title: Typed Cache Tensors Design Review, Round 2
eyebrow: Round-2 review of the REVISED codex design for issue #4525 (positron-ai/tron)
h1: Did the revised design for typed KV-cache tensors close the round-1 findings, and is it implementable now?
meta: Reviewed 2026-09-22 UTC by Claude (Fable 5.1) for jhan. Design reviewed: [status/design-new-tensor-type.html](design-new-tensor-type.html), revised by codex after the [round-1 review](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html) (revision finalized 2026-09-22 03:06 UTC, 83,567 bytes). Sources pinned to main f46e48ba (the design's snapshot), main 98bb8cb2 (the tip the design records), the live main tip 2880c3aa9b (fetched 2026-09-22 ~04:00 UTC, unchanged since 01:14 UTC) and PR 4424 head 30c4ac82cb.
short_version: The revision resolved 35 of the 58 round-1 findings, left 20 partly resolved, and deferred the 3 issue-body edits to jhan; nothing regressed.

Four new major gaps remain: the 8-lane build guidance orders code and test runs for a configuration whose baseline tests do not compile, the NaN test rule ignores that TRON_IGNORE_NAN is on in every production build, the child section never switches the K storage member to the new owner, and the definition of done depends on reviewer answers that have no place to be recorded.
Verdict: accept with changes. After those four edits and an honest status column in section 9, another agent can implement the parent from this page.

round 1, F.. and C.. ids

The revised design cites these ids in brackets, for example [F05]
N.. and M.. ids
new findings of this round: N.. from the eight finders, M.. from the completeness critic
issue #4525
the GitHub issue codex created for the parent PR; jhan edited its title and first sentence on 2026-09-22 00:10 UTC; unchanged since
KV cache, K, V
the saved key (K) and value (V) vectors of earlier tokens; attention reads them
page, slot, head, D

a page holds 64 token positions; a slot is the cache region of one layer (or of several layers that share it); a head is one attention head; D is the head size, the number of values per token per head (128 for PR 4424's models)
bf16
the 16-bit brain floating-point format used for cached K and V
AMX, AVX-512, 16-lane and 8-lane builds

AMX and AVX-512 are CPU instruction sets. tron's vector width TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 fp32 values with AVX-512 (the 16-lane build) and 8 without (the 8-lane build); the 8-lane build stores V row-major, so it has no pair-interleaved V
packed V (pair-interleaved V)
today's V storage in the 16-lane build: for each dimension, tokens 2p and 2p+1 sit next to each other. Element offset = (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2
native K
today's K storage: one token's D values consecutive in memory (row-major)
blocked packed K (VNNI K)
PR 4424's K storage for 128-dimension heads: two consecutive dimensions of one token share a 4-byte unit, and 16 tokens share one 64-byte line
expr, view, const_view, tensor

tron's expression interface (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp), its typed pointer views over regularly laid-out memory and their read-only form (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp), and its owning arrays (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp)
v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, v_vnni_row
the revised design's names for the packed-V owner (the aligned array inside the cache block), the typed rank-2 view over it, and its logical row expression
append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, copy_plane
the revised design's typed bulk operations: write one token's V row into the packed plane (even token zeroes its odd partner), read one row out, copy one token between planes, copy a whole plane
kv_block
the struct that holds K then V for one head of one slot in one page (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp)
set_v, get_v, append_v, scaled_v, v_data
today's V functions in kv_cache.hpp: write one token, read one token, copy one token between pages, compute the weighted V sum, and return the raw pointer of a V plane
save_v_impl
the model function (h/tron/models/model.hpp) that stores one token's V into the cache during a forward pass; it calls page::set_v
Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant

the rule in kv_cache.hpp that every even-token V write zeroes its odd partner row. The weighted sum reads a whole pair even when the token count is odd, and NaN times 0 is NaN, so the padding row must be zero
arena, book
an arena is one allocated memory region holding cache blocks; book is the class that owns the arenas and the pages
EAGLE
the speculative model; its cache adds one extra physical KV slot and a separate embedding buffer (x_data); it requires uniform geometry
GOF, page_info
group of four: four tokens of K and V staged for the FPGA's hardware KV cache; the staging code reaches a page's rows through the page_info callbacks in h/tron/gof.hpp (namespace tron::hardware)
CI, Nix test build, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_K_VNNI

CI is the automated build and test. The Nix test build is the required CI lane. The two CMake options compile the AMX attention kernels and PR 4424's K layout; the Nix lane sets neither. Issue #3997 tracks the AMX gap

The revision does all of it. The chain save_v_impl -> page::set_v -> append_v_row is stated three times (lines 252, 303, 354). The phrase "logical operations" no longer appears anywhere in the design text (grep finds zero matches). Line 229 states that there is no generic packed row.set(expr) in the parent at all, which is stronger than the round-1 request. The verification row at line 395 matches the recommended test. The factual claims check out at live main: h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2830-2832 has `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16` then `pg.template set_v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j, &vs[ix][kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size]);`, and line 2839 `pg.mark_v_complete(slot, static_cast<size_t>(j));` follows the head loop, so "Preserve completion notifications after the store" is right. dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked for a table with one row per existing accessor (page::k, set_v, get_v, v and v_ptr for the 8-lane build, v_data, kv_block::v_base, append_v, scaled_v), a decision on page::k_tensor, the call made by save_v_impl and by full.hpp's v_head_fn (the GOF callback that unpacks one V row into FPGA staging scratch) after the change, and a grep-checkable definition of done. The revision supplies exactly that table at lines 249-258, decides k_tensor is dropped (line 251), names both call chains (lines 252-253), and gives the search command (line 360). The checkable claims are right. page::set_v takes (slot, kv_head, i_page, pointer) in both its non-template and template forms [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1622-1660; file unchanged through 2880c3aa9b]. v_head_fn calls get_v<hardware_attention_geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, off, dest) and returns dest in the 16-lane build, and v_ptr in the 8-lane build [h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2652-2663]. page::append_v obtains both blocks through kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(storage_offset, kv_head) [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1879-1883]. kv_block::v_base is called only by page::v_data [kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1612], and v_data has one production caller, the AMX PV call in self_attention.hpp [h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1680-1682]; the design's rg command finds that caller, so "Remove after all callers migrate" is executable. The round-1 verifier's point that keeping get_v with a raw destination is weaker than the sketch's load_row(span) is answered by line 242 ("Wrap caller-owned scratch in an existing contiguous view; add no scratch-view type"). One small slip in the 8-lane row is reported below as a new minor ambiguity; it does not undo the finding's resolution.
dispositions.new_defect: Kind: (c) ambiguity. Claim: design.txt:254 says "The model's save path may forward through the unified typed set_v wrapper; its conversion remains the old row .set()." No page::set_v exists in the 8-lane build at main. The set_v and get_v declarations sit inside `#if TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16` [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1616-1672], and the `#else` branch (1674-1725) declares only v() and v_ptr(). save_v_impl's own `#else` branch calls `pg.template v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j).set(slice<geometry.kv.head_size>()(vs[ix].as_view(), kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size))` [h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2833-2837]. So "unified typed set_v wrapper" means adding a new 8-lane page::set_v overload, and "may" leaves the implementer to guess whether to add it and remove the model's #if/#else, or to leave both unchanged. Both routes give the same conversion (the existing row .set()), so the risk is low. Recommendation: replace "may forward" with a decision, for example: "Add an 8-lane page::set_v(slot, kv_head, i_page, typed row view) that forwards to v(...).set(); save_v_impl then calls set_v in both builds and its #if/#else is removed", or "Leave save_v_impl's #if/#else and the 8-lane v().set() path unchanged".

The checker's new minor ambiguity at :254 ("The model's save path may forward through the unified typed set_v wrapper") is real: no 8-lane page::set_v exists, and save_v_impl's `#else` branch calls `pg.template v<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head, j).set(slice<geometry.kv.head_size>()(vs[ix].as_view(), kv_head * geometry.kv.head_size))` [model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2833-2837]. votes.correction: Two additions to the checker's new minor ambiguity, no change of status. (1) Kind (c): the design already leans toward the first of the checker's two options. design.txt:245 says "The row-major V overload is a thin forwarder to existing contiguous .set()" and :180 says "The 8-lane forwarding wrapper retains its existing contiguous-row constraints", so an 8-lane append_v_row overload and an 8-lane page::set_v wrapper are intended. The fix is to change "may forward" at :254 to a decision: "Add an 8-lane page::set_v(slot, kv_head, i_page, typed row view) that forwards to v(...).set(); save_v_impl calls set_v in both builds and its #if/#else is removed." (2) Kind (c), same table: design.txt:253 says page::get_v should "Wrap or accept a typed destination", while :252 decides the matching question for set_v ("Replace the source pointer with a typed contiguous row view"). The "or" leaves get_v's parameter type to the implementer. Callers at 2880c3aa9b: full.hpp:2652-2657 passes a bf16* scratch; t/t_llama_unit.cpp:107 (a requires-expression with bf16*), :819 and :1575 (bf16 arrays), :2038, :2761, :2824 (float arrays), :2539 (tensor<head_size>.data.data(), float). dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked for (a) the chunk-to-pair mechanics, (b) the exact bf16_chunk override signature and how the expr base detects it, (c) the set/merge mechanics, (d) a sentence rejecting the stride-2 view, and, per the verifier corrections, (e) a note that a missed override is bit-exact but slower plus adding the bf16 read path to the generated-instruction comparison. The revision meets (a), (b), (c) and (d). Checked: the address rule "pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i" in bf16 elements matches the existing get_v loops, which load `_mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2)` while i steps 16 dimensions (kv_cache.hpp:2416-2418@f46e48bab498); even rows use `_mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16)` (:2420) and odd rows `_mm512_and_si512(both, 0xffff0000)` (:2424-2429); the bf16 reads narrow with `_mm512_cvtepi32_epi16` (:2454, :2462), so "narrow the selected halves for bf16 reads" is right. The override signature matches the base exactly: expr.hpp:110-117@f46e48bab498 declares `bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept` and tests `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)`; existing overrides use the same form (h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53, h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:367@f46e48bab498). The stride-2 rejection is right: the rank-1 view's chunk() gathers scalars and set() stores scalars when s0 != 1 (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:155-166, 186-204@f46e48bab498). The set/merge mechanics are covered by moving the set_v bodies and by deferring generic row.set (design.txt:229, 241, 277). Two slips remain. First, design.txt:221 "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" is factually wrong: only omitting the member is silent (then `&B::bf16_chunk` names the inherited base member and compares equal); a different parameter type, return type, const-qualification, an overload set, or a template makes the `!=` in the if-constexpr condition ill-formed, which is a hard compile error at expr.hpp:112, and a missing noexcept still compares unequal so the override is used. The round-1 verifier corrections said exactly this. Second, design.txt:398 calls the fallback "lossy"; fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) (h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498) is bit-exact for values that came from bf16 because chunk() widens by a 16-bit shift, the low 16 bits are zero, the NaN mask never fires, and `srli 16` plus `cvtepi32_epi16` returns the original bits; the cost is an extra convert, not a loss. Because the fallback is bit-exact, the bit-pattern checks at design.txt:396 and 398 cannot detect a missing override, and the objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 omits the bf16 read path, so item (e) is not met.
dispositions.residual: 1) Replace the last sentence of design.txt:221 with: "Omitting bf16_chunk silently selects the base's fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) path; a mismatched signature fails to compile at the base's member-pointer comparison [expr.hpp:112@f46e48bab498]." 2) In design.txt:398 replace "silently takes a lossy fallback" with "silently takes the fp32 round-trip fallback, which is bit-exact for stored bf16 but slower", and add "exact bf16 row reads (bf16_chunk)" to the inspected regions at design.txt:440 so the objdump comparison detects a missing override.
dispositions.new_defect: Kind: factual error. Claim: design.txt:221 says a bf16_chunk override with "a different signature can silently select conversion instead"; in fact a different signature is a compile error and only omitting the member is silent. Evidence: h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117@f46e48bab498 `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)`; comparing pointers to members with different function types has no common type and is ill-formed outside SFINAE, while a missing member makes `&B::bf16_chunk` name the base member (equal, silent fallback). The round-1 verifier corrections for F35 stated this. Recommendation: reword as given in the residual; the actionable guidance (use the exact signature) is already correct, so no implementation change follows.

Items (a)-(d) are met and I re-derived them. (a) "Read pair chunk i at pair_base + 2 * chunk_size * i" [design.txt:220] matches the existing get_v loops, which load `_mm512_load_si512(v_ptr + i * 2)` with v_ptr a bf16 pointer and i stepping 16 dimensions [kv_cache.hpp:2413-2418@f46e48bab498], i.e. 32 bf16 elements per 16-dimension chunk. Even rows use `_mm512_slli_epi32(both, 16)` [:2420], odd rows `_mm512_and_si512(both, hi_16_of_32)` [:2429], and the bf16 destinations narrow with `_mm512_cvtepi32_epi16` [:2454, :2462], matching design.txt:225. (b) `bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept` [design.txt:221] is exactly the base's form [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:111@f46e48bab498] and the existing overrides' form [h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53, h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:367@f46e48bab498]; detection is `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)` [expr.hpp:112]. (c) is covered by moving the set_v bodies into append_v_row and deferring generic row.set [design.txt:229, 241, 277]. (d) [design.txt:225] is right: the rank-1 view's chunk() gathers scalars and set() stores scalars when s0 != 1 [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:155-166, 186-204@f46e48bab498]. Item (e) is not met and the revision adds two factual slips. Slip 1: "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" [design.txt:221]. Only omitting the member is silent, because `&B::bf16_chunk` then names the inherited base member and the comparison is equal. A different parameter type, return type or const-qualification gives two pointer-to-member types with no common type, so the `!=` at expr.hpp:112 is a hard compile error whenever the base function is instantiated, and it is instantiated by every bf16 hardware-tensor consumer, which calls `rhs.bf16_chunk(i)` through `expr<B, N> const&` [dmatensor.hpp:272-276, 293-296@f46e48bab498]. A missing noexcept converts and compares unequal, so the override is used. Slip 2: "silently takes a lossy fallback" [design.txt:398]. The fallback fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field is saturated AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right 16 and narrows [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:96-109 (AVX-512) and :60-87 (AVX2)@f46e48bab498]. A packed row's chunk() leaves the low 16 bits zero (shift left 16, or mask 0xffff0000), so the correction never fires and the round trip returns the stored bits. The fallback is bit-exact and only slower, so the bit-pattern checks at design.txt:396 and :398 cannot detect a missing override. The objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 names appends, token copies, weighted sums and arena allocation/restore but not the bf16 read path, so the omission stays undetectable. I agree with partly.

dispositions.assessment: Round 1 (as narrowed by the verifiers) asked for four things: (a) the exact construction spelling with no parentheses or braces, (b) an explicit ban on std::construct_at(p), T() and T{} as value-initialization, (c) the call sites book::allocate_kv_group and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage named in prose, and (d) an executable check for unwanted clearing, plus the refinement that construction runs once per slot region and that the EAGLE region exists only under uniform geometry. Items (a), (b) and (c) are met exactly (design.txt:324-330). The enumeration is right and verified: retained/reclaimable bytes are n_pages times the sum over slots of n_kv_heads * (2 * 64 * head_size * 2) bytes [kv_cache.hpp:651-668, 1160-1166 @2880c3aa9b], so under uniform geometry the arena is an exact multiple of sizeof(kv_block_t) and the whole-arena array bound is correct; the uniform accessor indexes blocks[(slot.i * n_kv_heads + kv_head) * n_pages + pg] from one base [kv_cache.hpp:1283-1284], which the whole-arena array matches; storage_location and slot_base are described correctly [kv_cache.hpp:727-736, 1188-1198]; the zero-byte early return exists [kv_cache.hpp:1200]; restore allocates only the reclaimable arena [kv_cache.hpp:963-974]. The EAGLE bullet (design.txt:333) is accurate but incomplete: the EAGLE physical slot exists only when `eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0` [kv_cache.hpp:771] and calculate_allocation_sizes returns nullopt otherwise [kv_cache.hpp:1157-1158]; it lives in the retained arena after the active retained prefix [kv_cache.hpp:716-718, 733-735], so the uniform whole-arena array already covers it, and the heterogeneous path never has one. The bullet does not say this, so an implementer may add a dead EAGLE branch to the heterogeneous enumeration. Item (d) was met by a different means: the type-trait-only check was replaced by inspection of the optimized allocation/restore paths for memset or clearing loops (design.txt:337, 399, 441). That detects the failure mode but is a manual disassembly step rather than the executable poison-fill test the verifier asked for. The tensor.hpp:263 construct_at precedent warning is absent; the explicit ban at :329 covers its practical effect. Note, not a defect: the array form places element 0 at region_base without an array cookie only because kv_block_t is trivially destructible (Itanium ABI cookie rule), which design.txt:328 already requires.
dispositions.residual: (1) In design.txt:333 add: "The EAGLE KV slot exists only under uniform geometry (eagle_compatible requires layout_t::uniform_geometry, kv_cache.hpp:771) and lies in the retained arena after the active retained prefix, so the uniform whole-arena array already includes it; the heterogeneous path has no EAGLE slot." (2) Optional: in design.txt:399 add an executable check: "Add a t_llama_unit case that fills a 64-byte-aligned buffer with a poison byte, runs the chosen construction form over it, and requires every byte unchanged; the trivial-type traits cannot detect value-initialization."

dispositions.design_evidence:
design.txt:28 (Words row, UNCHANGED from round 1): "book, arena, EAGLE — book owns cache pages and their memory allocations. An arena is one allocated memory region. EAGLE is the speculative model with an additional cache storage region."
design.txt:322: "book keeps ownership of the retained and reclaimable byte arenas. A kv_block still contains K followed by V for one head and page."
design.txt:331: "For uniform geometry, construct one array over the just-allocated arena's complete contiguous block region. Its bound is the checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)."
design.txt:332: "For heterogeneous geometry, enumerate physical storage offsets once and select only slots in the just-allocated arena. Restoring the reclaimable arena must not restart objects in the retained arena."
design.txt:333: "Include the physical EAGLE KV slot once, with the primary geometry. Do not touch x_data, the separate EAGLE embedding buffer; it contains no KV blocks. Construction cannot rely solely on the logical active-slot loop, which omits that extra physical slot. [C01] [C09]"
design.txt:353 (step 2): "Check byte sizes, alignment, EAGLE storage, all geometries, and allocation failure."
design.txt:468 (section 9): "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 — Accepted; array extent clarified — ... Include EAGLE KV, exclude embeddings."
dispositions.assessment:
Round 1 asked for four things: (1) name the two EAGLE extras separately (one extra KV storage slot with the primary geometry at the end of the retained arena, and the embedding buffer x_data that holds no kv_block); (2) say that EAGLE requires uniform geometry, so the per-arena one-array construction already covers the extra slot; (3) say that restore re-allocates only the reclaimable arena, so the EAGLE slot is constructed once, in the constructor; (4) rewrite the Words row and add a clause about x_data to the 'both byte arenas' sentence (verifier narrowed: 'arena' is the code's word for the two KV regions, so only add the clause).

What the revision did, checked against kv_cache.hpp at live main 2880c3aa9b (file identical from c7844ca2ce through 2880c3aa9b):
- (1) is met in substance at design.txt:333. The EAGLE KV slot is a physical slot with the primary geometry [kv_cache.hpp:906-909 eagle_storage_offset() = kv_storage_offset(logical_slot_count()); :1326-1329 asserts geometry == layout_t::primary_geometry]. x_data is a separate DMA buffer holding embeddings, not kv_blocks [kv_cache.hpp:1131 `std::optional<hardware::unique_dma<uint8_t[]>> x_data;`, :1106-1113 allocated separately from the two arenas, :810-812 'Retained KV, reclaimable KV, and EAGLE embeddings are separate buffers']. The clause 'the logical active-slot loop ... omits that extra physical slot' is right: for_each_active_slot runs only slot < logical_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp:1242-1249].
- (4) is met: 'both byte arenas' became 'the retained and reclaimable byte arenas' (design.txt:322), and the x_data clause is at design.txt:333. The Words row at design.txt:28 was NOT rewritten and still names one unspecified 'additional cache storage region'.
- (3) is only implied: design.txt:332 says restore must not restart retained objects, and design.txt:333 says 'once'. The design never states that the EAGLE slot lives in the retained arena. In the code it does: storage_location returns reclaimable = false for offset.i == logical_slot_count, so the EAGLE slot is at offsets.values[logical_slot_count].retained [kv_cache.hpp:727-735], and arena_sizes adds one slot to result.retained when support_eagle [kv_cache.hpp:717-719]; restore_reclaimable_kv_storage re-allocates only the reclaimable arena [kv_cache.hpp:968].
- (2) is absent. The design nowhere says EAGLE requires uniform geometry. The code requires it: `eagle_compatible = layout_t::uniform_geometry && x_bytes > 0` [kv_cache.hpp:771] and `TRON_ASSERT(!support_eagle || eagle_compatible, "EAGLE cache views require uniform geometry and embedding storage")` [kv_cache.hpp:788-789]. Under the design's own rule (uniform geometry = one array over the whole arena, design.txt:331), the EAGLE slot is already covered, because the retained arena byte count includes it [kv_cache.hpp:717-719, :1161-1165].

Net: the buffer ambiguity is removed and the x_data rule is stated; the uniform-geometry precondition, the retained-arena location and the Words row are still missing. Grade: partly.

Round 1 (a note) asked the design to name the hooks for the construction pass: run it after allocate_kv_group succeeds, loop over physical storage offsets (including the EAGLE slot with the primary geometry), filter by layout_t::storage_location, place the array at slot_base, size it geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages (verifier correction 1), one array for the uniform case, skip zero-byte arenas, and name for_each_active_slot / fill_random as the precedent (verifier correction 3).

The revision meets the substance, and each checkable claim is right at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b: allocate_kv_group returns early on bytes == 0 and installs the arena with destination.emplace [kv_cache.hpp:1199-1208]; both the constructor [:1101-1102] and restore_reclaimable_kv_storage [:968] call it, and publishing happens afterwards in refresh_kv_blocks_alias [:1114, :971]; storage_location returns {reclaimable, byte_offset} [:727-735]; slot_base returns arena->get() + n_pages * byte_offset with a checked multiply [:1188-1197]; each slot's block count is specs[slot].geometry.n_kv_heads * blocks per head [:664-666] and the accessor indexes blocks[kv_head * n_pages + pg] [:1334], so geometry.n_kv_heads * n_pages per slot is right; the uniform accessor indexes one array across slots from kv_blocks_alias [:1284-1289], matching design.txt:331; the EAGLE slot is a physical offset beyond the logical slots with the primary geometry [:906-909, :1326-1329] and for_each_active_slot skips it [:1242-1249], matching design.txt:333.

I also checked the hook's precondition: storage_slot_count_ and support_eagle_ are set in the constructor's initializer list [kv_cache.hpp:1090-1093] before the body calls allocate_kv_group [:1101], so a slot loop inside allocate_kv_group can read logical_slot_count() and has_eagle_storage() safely.

On verifier correction (b) (do not implement as array placement-new): the design keeps `::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count]` (design.txt:326), which is the exact form the round-1 review page's edit list item 7 prescribed (prior-review.txt:1794). Per CWG 2382 (adopted in C++20; tron builds with CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23, CMakeLists.txt:56@2880c3aa9b), the non-allocating placement form may not add array overhead, and kv_block_t is trivially destructible, so no array cookie is needed under the Itanium ABI either. What is still unnamed: the loop bound storage_slot_count() [kv_cache.hpp:913-915], the EAGLE offset accessor eagle_storage_offset() [:906-909], and the fill_random precedent [:1058-1065]. The design links the code region that holds them and describes the loop precisely enough that an agent cannot guess wrong. Grade: resolved.

dispositions.assessment:
Round 1 asked for a child accessor table covering the five page members PR 4424 adds (k_vnni_plane, set_k_row, get_k_row, set_k_block, the !layout_on requires-clauses on page::k), an explicit statement that the typed store_block keeps its input shape (16 independent row pointers, null allowed for absent lanes, never a contiguous 16-row buffer), and a statement of where k_vnni_view is declared so kernels/k_vnni.hpp (included by kv_cache.hpp) does not create an include cycle with the tensor header.

The revision adds exactly that table [design.txt:374-381] and the header placement [design.txt:369]. Each row matches the child source. kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:1689 `const bf16* k_vnni_plane(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head) const noexcept` is the raw accessor the table removes. :1701-1705 set_k_row(slot, kv_head, i_page, const bf16* row) calls k_vnni::scatter_row; :1737-1741 get_k_row calls k_vnni::gather_row; the table keeps both names and moves the address math into the K type. :1723-1730 `set_k_block(kv_slot_id slot, size_t kv_head, size_t c, __mmask16 present, const bf16* const rows[k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16])` calls `k_vnni::store_block(plane, c, present, rows)`; the design's `store_block(view, block, mask, rows)` maps plane->view, c->block, present->mask one to one. The null-lane rule matches k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:186-187 "rows[t] points at the 128 bf16 of token t. It may be null for an absent token." and the signature at :194-197. The page::k overloads at kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:1619-1674 all carry `!k_vnni::layout_on<...>`, which the table keeps. qk_group, named in the "Copy and score readers" row, is the AVX-512 reader at k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:248 (the "software score reader" of design.txt:369).

The include-cycle answer is sound. kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:27 includes tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp; k_vnni.hpp includes only <immintrin.h> and common/ headers (:32-40); the tensor headers include kernels/expr.hpp and kernels/chunky.hpp (view.hpp@2880c3aa9b:6, views.hpp:6) but no kernels/k_vnni.hpp. So the proposed chain tensor/k_vnni.hpp <- kernels/k_vnni.hpp <- kv_cache.hpp has no cycle. h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp exists at neither 30c4ac82cbb6 nor 2880c3aa9b, so it is a new file as the design intends. Two headers share the basename k_vnni.hpp in different directories; tron already does this (h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp and common/numerics/bf16.hpp), and the design always writes full paths, so this is not a defect.

The section 9 row "accessor changes" describes this fix accurately.

Line 401 adds the verification entry. The ambiguous bridging sentence is removed. Factual claims in the new text check out against the child source. The child's row store is a 4-byte-lane scatter: scatter_row calls _mm512_i32scatter_epi32 [h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:139-143]. The block store is lane-masked for a partial block (_mm512_mask_storeu_epi32) and a plain full-line store for a full block [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:206-213]; a full-line store without a prior read is not a read-modify-write, so it does not contradict line 383. Note [Shared block save] exists [h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2732] and says "Their writers use masked stores on disjoint token lanes. So two threads may write one block without conflict." [model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2763-2765]. Note [K VNNI storage] exists [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:653]. The mixed case the rule protects is real: a run of one token goes through set_k_row (scatter) while other units of the same block go through set_k_block (masked store), both inside one shared window [model.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:2914-2941]. dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked for a written procedure: a named baseline, the build flags, a disassembly tool, the code to inspect, and a definition of a material change. The verifier corrections narrowed this: name the tool, say that the targeted functions are always-inline so the comparison unit is the inlined call site, map the configurations to CMake flags, gather the criteria in one place, and adopt neither a numeric threshold nor a default timing campaign. The revision does each of these. The baseline is the parent's main baseline commit built with the same preset and flags (design.txt:439). The tool is objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn -C on the t_llama_unit binary (design.txt:440); those are valid GNU binutils flags. The configuration is named by reference to the table (16-lane, AMX on = cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=ON, design.txt:412); the CMake option names are right (CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:44 option(AVX512 ...), :48 option(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH ...)) and the native preset builds RelWithDebInfo (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:31-34). The always-inline warning is correct: page::set_v is declared TRON(inline) (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48ba:1621 and the definition at :2288), append_v is TRON(inline) (:1872), scaled_v_expr::accumulate_16_chunks is TRON(inline) (:2010), and TRON(inline) expands to tron_inline = inline __attribute__((always_inline)) (h/common/attributes.hpp@2880c3aa9b:24,78). The instruction named for the weighted V sum is right: scaled_v_expr uses _mm512_dpbf16_ps, whose mnemonic is vdpbf16ps (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48ba:2019-2034, 2087-2090). t_llama_unit is a valid object to inspect: it includes model.hpp and kv_cache.hpp and instantiates scaled_v and set_v (t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:65-66, 1665-1723). The material-change criteria are consolidated in one sentence (design.txt:442), timing is conditional rather than default (design.txt:443), and no numeric threshold is claimed (design.txt:445), as the verifiers asked. The design's [F17] and [C..] bracket citations link to the round-1 page, and the section 9 row records the disposition. The finding is met on substance.

dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked the design to name the formatting command, the static checks, the targeted test binaries, the suite gate and the benchmark-refresh command. The verifier corrections adjusted the list: add make lint, which is a required CI check name; treat make iwyu-check as optional because the parent's headers are not public API headers under the repository's own definition; and note that bin/slice bench writes only the detected platform's block of config/test-benchmarks.json. The revision names make format, make iwyu-check, make build-test, make test-host (design.txt:431), bin/slice route (:429), nix develop --accept-flake-config (:430) and bin/slice bench --update t_llama_unit (:432). All of these targets exist: GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b format at :819, iwyu-check at :984, build-test at :351, test-host at :905; the skill text at .agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:55-56, 65-66, 69-70 matches. The targeted binaries are named in step 6 (design.txt:357) and the behavior table (:400). Two of the verifier adjustments were not taken. First, make lint is absent, although lint is the check the repository actually requires: README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:76-78 lists Lint among the checks branch protection must require, :92-93 lists lint among the legacy required check names, and :655-659 ("Reproducing CI Locally") runs make build-test, make format, make lint; the lint target (GNUmakefile:693-696) is the one that fails on trailing whitespace and tells the developer to run make format. Second, make iwyu-check is listed under "required checks" although README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b contains no IWYU check (grep for iwyu returns nothing) and SKILL.md:65-66 ties it only to a public API header, which the parent does not touch (round-1 verifier: AGENTS.md:71-72 and h/libtron.hpp:14-17 define the public API as four IWYU-exported headers). Running iwyu-check is harmless, but calling it required while omitting lint would make an implementing agent skip the one check CI enforces. Third, the platform-keyed bench file is not mentioned: bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1731-1736 put_platform_bench writes only the current host's platform block, so a run on delphi-3bda refreshes only the granite_rapids_6962p entry. The whole-machine qualifier on bench is correct (bin/slice:1983-2002). The formatting command, the main omission, is now named; the check list needs one addition and one relabel.

Evidence: README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:76-78 (branch protection must require Lint, ..., Test host, ...), :92-93 (legacy required check names build, lint, test, test-fpga, test-host, ci-machinery-tests), :655-659 (local reproduction runs make build-test, make format, make lint); README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b has no IWYU check; SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:65-66 requires make iwyu-check only for "A public API header", and the parent edits none (AGENTS.md:71-72, h/libtron.hpp:14-17 per round-1 verifier). dispositions.design_evidence: design.txt:83: "A packed-V weighted sum rounds an odd live-token count up to a complete pair. The unused odd row must be zero: a NaN multiplied by a zero weight still contaminates the sum. The row-major path reads exactly the live-token count. [S5]". design.txt:85-93 (the new figure): "Reused pair Old even row Odd row: NaN poison" -> "Append even token New even values Odd row: all zero" -> "Append odd token Even values preserved New odd values". design.txt:95: "The even append must clear the partner every time the pair is reused. This is an operation sequence, not a timing diagram." design.txt:97-101 (table): "Even cache append | No | Odd row becomes zero", "Odd cache append | Yes, pair must be initialized | Even row is preserved", "Direct element update | No read of other elements required | Other elements unchanged; this does not establish cache readiness". design.txt:473: "draw the poisoned-pair reuse sequence".
dispositions.assessment: Round 1 was a note. Its recommendation asked to replace the third flow diagram (even -> completion -> odd label boxes) with a two-lane figure (even cell, odd cell of one pair) over the operation sequence, including page reuse with a stale odd row, and optionally to shrink diagrams 1 and 2. The round-1 verifiers kept diagrams 1 and 2 (they show hierarchy and sequencing) and called the new figure optional polish. The revision replaces diagram 3 with a `.pairfigure` element (HTML lines 232-240): three stages, each drawn as two cells (even row, odd row), with the odd cell colored orange for "NaN poison" and green for "all zero". The figure has role="img" and an aria-label that states the mechanism. The stale-odd-row-on-reuse case, which round 1 said was missing, is now the first stage. A new three-row table (design.txt:97-101) adds the case the figure does not draw: a direct element update preserves the other elements and does not establish cache readiness. Diagrams 1 and 2 are kept (HTML lines 79 and 97), consistent with the verifiers' reading. Two optional items from the round-1 recommendation are not drawn: the weighted sum (scaled_v_expr) reading the zero odd cell when the live count is odd, and a red mark on that step. Both are stated in the sentence directly above the figure (design.txt:83). Since the round-1 verifiers classed the figure as optional and the implementing agent needs no change, this counts as resolved on substance. The figure is still CSS boxes, not SVG; that is not a defect.

dispositions.design_evidence: design.txt:318: "Packed set_v can turn an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits into infinity when it discards the lower bits. Generic fp32s_to_bf16s, the expression conversion helper, sets the lowest retained mantissa bit when the exponent is all ones and discarded bits are nonzero. It skips that correction when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined. This preserves a NaN but does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN. Neither path rounds to nearest. Preserve each existing path separately. [S5] [S7]". design.txt:313-314: "Packed V append from bf16 | Preserve exact input bits. No float round trip." / "Packed V append from fp16 / float | Keep today's conversion to fp32 and upper-16-bit truncation. Do not substitute general expression conversion." design.txt:396 (test row): "Use independently specified expected bit patterns around truncation boundaries, infinity, and NaN. Verify bf16 bulk load/copy exactly. Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate." design.txt:474: "F41 | Accepted; example corrected | Preserve packed/generic conversion differences. Limit the NaN-to-infinity example to fp32 input; the review's fp16 example omitted instruction-level NaN handling."
dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked for three things: state the exact NaN divergence rule, give the worked example (fp32 0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80 = +Inf under the packed set_v truncation, 0x7F81 under fp32s_to_bf16s), and tell the test author that expected bits differ per path and per build type (TRON_IGNORE_NAN). The round-1 verifiers withdrew the fp16 example (the hardware fp16-to-fp32 conversion quiets the NaN first), and the design's section 9 row records that correctly. The revised rule text at design.txt:318 is factually right on every checkable point. fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic fp32-to-bf16 conversion) ORs 0x00010000 into any lane whose exponent field is 0x7f800000 and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right by 16 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:62-71 (AVX2) and 92-109 (AVX-512) @f46e48bab498; the file is unchanged at 2880c3aa9b]. Bit 16 becomes bf16 bit 0, the lowest mantissa bit, not the quiet bit, so "does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN" is right. Both bodies are wrapped in #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN and skip the correction when it is defined [bf16.hpp:57-58 and 93-95 @f46e48bab498]. Two parts of the recommendation are still missing. (1) No worked example: the text says "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits" but never gives 0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 versus 0x7F81, and "no upper mantissa bits" is loose (it means fp32 mantissa bits 22 to 16 all zero). (2) The build-type consequence is absent: TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:267-270 @f46e48bab498; 292-295 and 314-317 @2880c3aa9b: "$<$<AND:${CXX_GccOrClang},$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>>:-O3;-DTRON_IGNORE_NAN;-DTRON_IGNORE_FTZ>"], and the required Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 @2880c3aa9b]. So in CI and production both paths truncate identically, and a hard-coded NaN expectation for the generic (8-lane row-view .set()) path passes in one build type and fails in the other. The test row at design.txt:396 says only "Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate", which does not warn the implementing agent about the build-type dependence. This is the part with a practical consequence, so the finding is partly addressed.
dispositions.residual: At design.txt:318 replace "an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits" with "an fp32 NaN whose upper 7 mantissa bits (bits 22-16) are zero, for example 0x7F800001, which set_v stores as 0x7F80 (+Inf) and fp32s_to_bf16s stores as 0x7F81 when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is not defined". Add one sentence: "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug build (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt, the tron target_compile_options generator expression), including the RelWithDebInfo Nix test build, so outside Debug both paths truncate identically." In the test row at design.txt:396 add: "NaN expected bits for the generic conversion path depend on CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE (TRON_IGNORE_NAN); either test both cases under #ifdef or restrict NaN cases to the packed append path, which always truncates."

votes.reason: The revised rule sentence (design.txt:318) is factually right on every point I checked: fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic fp32-to-bf16 conversion) ORs 0x00010000 into any lane whose exponent field equals 0x7f800000 and whose low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right by 16 [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:56-71 (AVX2) and 92-109 (AVX-512) @f46e48bab498; git diff f46e48bab498..2880c3aa9b shows no change to that file]. Bit 16 becomes bf16 bit 0, the lowest mantissa bit, not the quiet bit (bf16 bit 6), so "does not necessarily make it a quiet NaN" is right. The correction is skipped under #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN [bf16.hpp:57-58, 93-95]. Two parts of the round-1 recommendation remain missing. (1) No worked example (0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 = +Inf under set_v truncation, 0x7F81 under fp32s_to_bf16s); grep of design.txt finds no 0x7F8 pattern. (2) No build-type consequence: TRON_IGNORE_NAN is set by `target_compile_options(tron PUBLIC ...)` for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295 @2880c3aa9b, and again at 314-317 on tron_model_compile_config], PUBLIC means every test executable that links tron inherits it (t_llama_unit links tron, t/CMakeLists.txt:610-616 @f46e48bab498 per facts-r1), and the required Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 @2880c3aa9b]. So in CI both paths truncate identically, and a hard-coded NaN expectation for the generic (row-view .set()) path passes in Debug and fails in CI, or the reverse. grep of design.txt finds no "Debug", "RelWithDebInfo" or "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE"; TRON_IGNORE_NAN appears only at line 318, without saying when it is defined. The test row (design.txt:396) says only "Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate". Existing precedent the design could point to: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-99 @2880c3aa9b already warns "this test may fail on some hardware if IGNORE_NAN is set" and uses only quiet NaNs (inf-inf, 0/0), which survive truncation on both paths.
votes.correction: The checker's residual is right; add two facts to it. First, say that TRON_IGNORE_NAN is a PUBLIC compile option of the tron target [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-295 @2880c3aa9b], so test executables that link tron compile with it too; otherwise a reader may think only library code is affected. Second, in the test-row addition, name the existing precedent: t/t_bf16.cpp:97-99 @2880c3aa9b ("bf16 preserves nan") avoids the build-type dependence by using quiet NaNs only (inf-inf and 0/0, bit 22 set), so the design can say: use quiet NaNs for expectations shared by both paths, and put the signalling-NaN case (0x7F800001) only on the packed append path, which always truncates.

votes.reason: Round 1 asked for three things: the exact NaN divergence rule, a worked example, and per-path expected bits for the test author; the verifiers added that the divergence exists only when TRON_IGNORE_NAN (a compile-time define) is not set, and that the test row must say so [r1-findings.md F41 Recommendation and Verifier corrections 2-4]. The rule is now stated and is correct: design.txt:318 says packed set_v (the cache's V write) can turn an fp32 NaN with no upper mantissa bits into infinity, that fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic fp32-to-bf16 conversion) sets the lowest retained mantissa bit when the exponent is all ones and the discarded bits are nonzero, and that it skips this when TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined. I confirmed each clause against h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:57-71 (AVX2) and 93-108 (AVX-512) at 2880c3aa9b, where the OR of 0x00010000 is inside #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN / #else and the shift right by 16 follows; the file is unchanged from f46e48bab498 (git diff --stat empty). The per-path guidance is met in substance by the table rows at design.txt:312-314 (row-major V keeps row-view .set() conversion; packed V from fp16/float keeps fp32 conversion plus upper-16-bit truncation), and view::set does call chunky<bf16,true>::set, which calls fp32s_to_bf16s [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:191 and h/tron/kernels/chunky.hpp:55-57 @2880c3aa9b]. Two concrete parts are missing. First, no worked example: neither 0x7F800001 nor 0x7F80/0x7F81 appears anywhere in design.txt (grep for 0x7F returns nothing), although the section 9 row says "example corrected" [design.txt:474]. Second, the build-type consequence is absent: TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration [src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:293 and 316 @2880c3aa9b; :268 @f46e48bab498], and the Nix test build is RelWithDebInfo [nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 @2880c3aa9b], so in CI and production both paths truncate identically and a hard-coded NaN expectation for the generic path passes in Debug only. The test row at design.txt:396 says only "Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate" and does not warn about this. design.txt contains no occurrence of Debug, RelWithDebInfo or CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE.
votes.correction: The checker's residual is right. Add one item: the section 9 row for F41 [design.txt:474] says "Accepted; example corrected", but the design text contains no worked example at all, so either insert the fp32 example the checker proposes at design.txt:318 or change the row to say the example was removed. Also state the direction plainly for the test author: with TRON_IGNORE_NAN defined (all non-Debug builds, including the required Nix RelWithDebInfo build) fp32s_to_bf16s gives 0x7F80 for input 0x7F800001, the same as set_v; only a Debug build gives 0x7F81.

dispositions.design_evidence: design.txt:272: "Keep amx_attn_iface.hpp free of processor intrinsics. Forward-declare the packed view and the existing five-parameter view/const_view templates. Spell native dimensions and strides with std::integer_sequence, or share a small intrinsics-free declarations header." design.txt:273: "seq and sseq are aliases, not class templates that can be forward-declared. Do not repeat template defaults. Include complete tensor definitions only where callers or function definitions need them, including the fake AMX definitions. [Header-boundary finding]" design.txt:355 (step 4): "h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp, h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp | Use typed cache arguments. Keep the interface header free of intrinsics." design.txt:260-266 (kernel declarations): "void qk_rowmajor_128x4( const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page, ..." / "void weights_times_v_128x4( v_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> v_page, ...". design.txt:202-205: "template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> using native_k_view = view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>; template <size_t Rows, size_t Cols> using const_native_k_view = const_view<bf16, true, false, seq<Rows, Cols>>;". design.txt:475: "F43 | Accepted; declaration advice corrected | Keep the interface header intrinsics-free. seq and sseq are aliases; forward-declare the actual view classes with explicit shape and stride types."
dispositions.assessment: Round 1 asked the design to say how amx_attn_iface.hpp (the AMX kernel interface header, documented as containing no intrinsics) obtains the new parameter type names: forward-declare the view templates instead of including the tensor header, and include full headers only in amx_attn.cpp and the fake test translation units. The round-1 verifiers added that seq cannot be forward-declared (it is an alias template) and that the default Stride argument lives only in views.hpp, so a bare forward declaration cannot supply it. The revision adopts the forward-declaration route and incorporates both corrections. Every checkable claim holds. view and const_view are five-parameter templates with a defaulted fifth parameter, Stride = row_major<Dim> [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36 @2880c3aa9b]. seq and sseq are alias templates over std::integer_sequence [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:22 and 25 @2880c3aa9b], so "seq and sseq are aliases" is right, and spelling them as std::integer_sequence<size_t,...> and std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t,...> names the same types. row_major<seq<64,128>> is sseq<128,1> [seq.hpp:388-394 and the static_assert at 510-511 @2880c3aa9b], so an explicit stride spelling is possible. "Do not repeat template defaults" is the C++ rule; g++ 11.4 on this host rejects a repeated default with "redefinition of default argument for 'class U'", and accepts a bare forward declaration followed by a definition that adds the default. A forward-declared class is a valid by-value parameter type in a function declaration (confirmed with g++ 11.4), so the kernel declarations at design.txt:260-266 compile against forward declarations. expr.hpp:17-22 @2880c3aa9b already forward-declares view and const_view without the default, which is the precedent round 1 named. amx_attn_iface.hpp already includes common/numerics/bf16.hpp [amx_attn_iface.hpp:112 @f46e48bab498], so the name bf16 is available there. With forward declarations the header comment "contains no intrinsics" [amx_attn_iface.hpp:2-5 @f46e48bab498] and the "// intrinsics-free" tag [self_attention.hpp:21 @2880c3aa9b] stay accurate, so no comment update is needed. One note, no change required: seq.hpp itself is intrinsics-free (its includes are <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp, common/numerics/std.hpp @2880c3aa9b, none of which pulls tron/simd.hpp), so amx_attn_iface.hpp may include tron/tensor/seq.hpp and write seq<>/sseq<> directly instead of spelling std::integer_sequence; the design's second option, a shared declarations header, covers this.
dispositions.new_defect: Kind: (c) ambiguity. Claim: the revised text does not say in which header the alias templates native_k_view and const_native_k_view are defined, and the two places that use them are incompatible under the design's own rules. Evidence: design.txt:202-205 writes the aliases with four template arguments, which relies on the default Stride = row_major<Dim> that only views.hpp:22-36 @2880c3aa9b supplies. design.txt:260-261 uses const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> inside amx_attn_iface.hpp. design.txt:272-273 tells the implementer to forward-declare view/const_view there without repeating the default. After a bare forward declaration `template <typename T, bool aligned, bool dma, typename Dim, typename Stride> struct const_view;` the four-argument alias does not compile (g++ 11.4 on this host: "wrong number of template arguments (1, should be 2)" on the equivalent two-parameter test). If the implementer instead writes the alias in amx_attn_iface.hpp with the explicit five-argument spelling and keeps the four-argument alias in the tensor header, the alias template is declared twice; g++ 11.4 accepts an identical alias-template redeclaration, but the pinned compiler is clang 19 (facts-r2: flake.nix llvmStdenv), which is not available on this host, so whether that compiles is Insufficient data. Recommendation: add one sentence to design.txt:272-273 naming a single header that defines native_k_view and const_native_k_view exactly once (the "small intrinsics-free declarations header" the design already offers, holding the forward declarations of view, const_view and v_vnni_view plus the two aliases with the stride spelled explicitly or with tron/tensor/seq.hpp included), and state that both amx_attn_iface.hpp and h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp include it.

votes.reason: The revision does answer the round-1 omission (how amx_attn_iface.hpp, the AMX kernel interface header, gets the parameter type names): forward-declare the packed view and the five-parameter view/const_view templates, spell shape and stride with std::integer_sequence or share a small intrinsics-free declarations header, do not repeat template defaults (design.txt:272-273). Every C++ fact in it checks out: view and const_view are five-parameter templates with Stride = row_major<Dim> defaulted [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36 @2880c3aa9b]; seq and sseq are alias templates [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:21-25 @2880c3aa9b]; expr.hpp:17-22 @2880c3aa9b is the forward-declaration precedent; amx_attn_iface.hpp:1-5 @f46e48bab498 documents "no intrinsics" and line 112 already includes common/numerics/bf16.hpp; self_attention.hpp:21 @2880c3aa9b carries the "// intrinsics-free" tag. But the round-1 verifier correction (b) asked the design to pick one route AND make the const_native_k_view alias consistent with it, and the revision does not. Three statements cannot be followed together: the alias is defined with four arguments, relying on the default Stride (design.txt:202-205); the sample kernel declaration inside the interface header uses that alias, const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> (design.txt:260-261); and line 272 says to forward-declare without the default and spell strides with std::integer_sequence. Compile probes with g++ 11.4 (the only compiler on this host; the pinned clang 19 is absent, so clang behaviour is Insufficient data): (a) the four-argument alias after a bare five-parameter forward declaration fails, "wrong number of template arguments (4, should be 5)"; (b) an alias named const_native_k_view spelled with std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, C, 1> next to the tensor header's four-argument alias fails, "conflicting declaration of template"; (c) an alias spelled row_major<seq<R,C>> coexists with the four-argument alias, and a forward-declared class works as a by-value parameter with the default added later. self_attention.hpp includes both amx_attn_iface.hpp (line 21) and kv_cache.hpp (line 27) @2880c3aa9b, so any TU including it would see both spellings. An implementing agent following line 272 literally therefore hits a compile error at the first build. Kind (c) ambiguity, severity minor (caught by the compiler, not a wrong design). Because this is the exact point round 1 raised, I grade F43 partly rather than resolved plus a separate new defect.
votes.correction: Fold the checker's "new defect" into F43's residual instead of listing it separately, and sharpen it with the probe result: spelling the stride as std::integer_sequence<ptrdiff_t, Cols, 1> under the alias name const_native_k_view conflicts with the four-argument alias (g++ 11.4: "conflicting declaration of template"), while row_major<seq<Rows, Cols>> does not. Recommended text for design.txt:272-273: define native_k_view and const_native_k_view exactly once, in one intrinsics-free declarations header that includes tron/tensor/seq.hpp (its includes are <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp and common/numerics/std.hpp @2880c3aa9b, none of which reaches tron/simd.hpp), forward-declares view, const_view and v_vnni_view without defaults, and spells the stride as row_major<seq<Rows, Cols>>; state that both h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp and h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp include that header; and remove the "std::integer_sequence" option from line 272, or limit it to function parameter types, never to the alias name.

The revision adopts forward declarations and both corrections [design.txt:272-273; step 4 at design.txt:355]. Every checkable claim holds at live main 2880c3aa9b. view and const_view are five-parameter struct templates with Stride = row_major<Dim> as default [h/tron/tensor/views.hpp:22-36]. seq and sseq are alias templates over std::integer_sequence [h/tron/tensor/seq.hpp:21-25], so "seq and sseq are aliases" is right. row_major<seq<R,C>> expands to sseq<C,1> [seq.hpp:387-394, static_assert at 510-511], so an explicit stride spelling exists. I compiled the C++ rules with g++ 11.4 from stdin (no files written): a repeated default after a forward declaration that already has one is rejected ("redefinition of default argument"), which supports design.txt:273; a bare forward declaration followed by a definition that adds the default compiles; a five-argument alias plus a by-value parameter of the still-incomplete view type in a function declaration compiles, so the signatures at design.txt:260-266 are valid against forward declarations. seq.hpp includes only <algorithm>, <type_traits>, <utility>, common/assert.hpp, common/attributes.hpp and common/numerics/std.hpp [seq.hpp:3-9], so it is itself intrinsics-free, as the checker notes. dispositions.assessment:
Round 1 asked section 6 to name the two scheduler rules that encode the V pair layout outside the cache: adjust_grains_for_partners (the minibatch splitter in model.hpp that keeps the even and odd token of a pair in one minibatch) and token_ix_needed (the page-readiness check in common.hpp). It asked the design to say both stay in place, to reword the model.hpp comment that names page.set_v if set_v changed, and to state that the Definition of done forbids physical address arithmetic outside the tensor, not layout knowledge in the scheduler.

The revision does the substance of this. Line 305 names both functions and their files, keeps both, and says their layout knowledge stays outside the tensor. Line 450 limits the Definition of done to physical addresses. Step 3 (line 354) lists model.hpp and the common.hpp comments as the files.

I checked the names and files at live main. adjust_grains_for_partners is called at h/tron/models/model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:214 and :252 and defined at :264; the comment at :209-213 still says "because `page.set_v` interleaves them in the same SIMD values". token_ix_needed is at h/tron/models/common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1024-1036 with the comment "scaled_v reads the entire page, including masked-out entries, and V writes share interleaved storage. Wait for every producer of a page that any query sees". At the design's snapshot the older page-level version is at common.hpp@f46e48bab498:949-958. Names and files in the design are right.

Two slips. (a) Factual: "token_ix_needed, the partner-readiness rule" is a mislabel. The function decides whether a minibatch depends on token tok by scanning every visible range of the page that contains tok [common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1028-1035]. It has no even/odd or partner logic. It is a page-readiness rule; the pair rule is adjust_grains_for_partners. (c) Ambiguity: "Update their explanatory comments" applies to both functions but says what neither comment should say. The token_ix_needed comment stays true after the parent (scaled_v still reads whole pages, design.txt:316), so nothing needs to change there; the round-1 verifier said both comments stay unchanged. The model.hpp:211 comment names page.set_v, and the revised design keeps page::set_v by name and makes it forward to append_v_row (design.txt:252), so that comment also stays literally true; an update is optional and the design gives no replacement text. Line numbers are not given, but the design tells the implementer to relocate citations on fetched main (design.txt:120), and function names are stable, so that is acceptable.
dispositions.residual: In design.txt:305 replace "the partner-readiness rule" with "the page-readiness rule (it waits for every producer of a page that any query sees, because scaled_v reads whole pages and V writes share interleaved storage)". Replace "Update their explanatory comments." with "Leave the token_ix_needed comment unchanged. In the adjust_grains_for_partners comment (model.hpp:209-213 at 2880c3aa9b) optionally add that page::set_v forwards to append_v_row, which does the pair interleaving." In step 3 (design.txt:354) either drop "comments in h/tron/models/common.hpp" from the Files column or say the common.hpp comment needs no change.
dispositions.new_defect: Kind (a) factual error. Claim: the revision labels token_ix_needed "the partner-readiness rule" (design.txt:305); the function has no partner or pair logic. Evidence: h/tron/models/common.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1024-1036 scans every visible range of the page containing tok and its comment says "Wait for every producer of a page that any query sees"; the pair rule is adjust_grains_for_partners at model.hpp@2880c3aa9b:209-214, 264. Risk: the same sentence tells the implementer to "Update their explanatory comments", so an agent following the label could write a wrong "partner" comment into common.hpp. Recommendation: call it the page-readiness rule and state that its comment stays unchanged.

confirmed.title: Both-chunk-width rule forces unused 8-lane packed bodies
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design, Build and include boundaries; 8. Verification, Build configurations
confirmed.claim: Design decision I disagree with, plus an ambiguity: the rule to compile the packed types under both chunk widths and to derive the pair-chunk width from chunk_size makes the implementing agent write AVX2 (8-lane) bodies for append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, chunk and bf16_chunk, and run the packed-V test rows in the 8-lane configuration, for a layout the 8-lane cache never uses. Only class completeness is required there: the fake kernel takes the view by value, and completing a class template instantiates the class body, not its member function bodies. AMX dispatch is a compile error in the 8-lane build, so no 8-lane code calls any packed operation. The test rows in section 8 are not chunk-guarded, so t_llama_unit would instantiate the bodies at 8 lanes unless the agent guesses to guard them.

In the 8-lane (AVX2) build no caller exists for the packed row reads: the AMX dispatch is rejected by a preprocessor error when TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16, and the unconditionally compiled fakes need only a complete class, not instantiated member bodies. confirmed.claim: Omission: the design says the generic conversion skips its NaN correction when TRON_IGNORE_NAN (the compile-time switch that disables NaN handling in the SIMD conversion helpers) is defined, but it does not say when that happens. All three configurations in the design's section 8 table use `cmake --preset native`, and the native preset is RelWithDebInfo. The required Nix CI build is also RelWithDebInfo. In every one of those builds fp32s_to_bf16s (the generic bf16 conversion) truncates exactly like the packed set_v path, so 0x7F800001 becomes 0x7F80 (+Inf) on both paths. Only the Debug presets asan, tsan and coverage produce the 0x7F81 result the design's paragraph describes. The section 8 row 'Keep packed append and generic expression conversion expectations separate' therefore cannot be implemented with fixed NaN expectations: a value chosen from the design's prose passes in Debug and fails under `--preset native` and in required CI, or the reverse. The round-1 F41 verifier correction stated this dependence explicitly; the revised text carries only the conditional clause.

votes.reason: I re-derived the finding from the primary sources and it holds. (1) The omission is real. The reviewer-question table has exactly two columns, "Question" and "Proposed answer" [design.txt:80-85]. A grep of the whole design text for "No", "otherwise", "alternative", "fall back" and "sketch" finds no sentence that maps a No answer to the sections that would change; the only alternative named is indirect ("In the sketch, the layout is a template argument of both the owner and the view", design.txt:59; "It avoids a public layout-policy template", design.txt:62). The design does gate implementation on the answers: section 8's acceptance list says "The reviewer questions have recorded answers, and the implemented interface matches them" [design.txt:449], and section 9 marks F02/F03/F04/F26/F51/F52 as "Accepted; reviewer answers pending" [design.txt:464]. So an implementer who receives a No has no guidance, which is what the finding says. Round-1 F02 asked codex to list the questions and mark the design conditional [r1-findings.md:20]; it did not ask for the consequence of a No, so N07 is a new round-2 point, not a re-raise of an addressed one. (2) The four per-question consequences check out against the sources. Q1: the sketch's alternative is `vnni_view<T, Layout>` / `vnni_tensor<Layout>` with the address formula in a layout struct (Ben comment 5765866077, github-review.json; facts-r1.md:29), which would replace the per-layout declarations at design.txt:198-205. Q2: Ben's rule is "As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const. vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does" (github-review.json, comment 5765866077); a No inverts "Const matrix access yields a read-only row" [design.txt:218] and "Return read-only element access" [design.txt:219] and removes the "const-row mutation" item of the compile check [design.txt:397]. Q3: at live main 2880c3aa9b, `expr<B, d, ds...>::operator[]` (both overloads) returns `self()[i]` [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:57-65@2880c3aa9b], and `tensor(expr<B, d0, d1, ds...> const& rhs)` constructs each row from `rhs[i]` [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp:272-274@2880c3aa9b]; a derived view without operator[] makes both fail to instantiate, so expression reads and the "Expression reads" test row [design.txt:398] cannot exist. Ben's sketch indeed has only `at()` and says "There is no data(), pointer conversion, or operator[] that suggests a contiguous row" (github-review.json, comment 5765866077). Q4: the deferred list is at design.txt:277-279 ("Explicitly deferred ... No packed slices or iterators; no generic row.set ..."), and a No to "Is the smaller parent scope sufficient?" [design.txt:85] puts it back in scope. One precision (not a refutation): only the const-object clauses of rows 218-219 invert on a Q2 No; the clause "An explicitly read-only row always rejects mutation" [design.txt:219] and the "Reject read-only writes" compile check [design.txt:397] depend on T = const bf16, which Ben's rule also keeps, so they are unaffected.
votes.correction: Narrow the Q2 clause: a No to Q2 inverts the const-object rules in the two contract rows (design.txt:218 "Const matrix access yields a read-only row"; design.txt:219 "Return read-only element access") and removes the "const-row mutation" item of the compile check at design.txt:397. The clause "An explicitly read-only row always rejects mutation" (design.txt:219) and the "Reject read-only writes" check stay, because they depend on the template argument T = const bf16, which Ben's std::span rule also keeps ("vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does"). confirmed.title: bf16_chunk 'different signature silently selects conversion' is wrong
confirmed.section: 5. Interface design (operation table) and 8. Verification (Expression reads row)
confirmed.claim: Factual error: the revision repeats the claim that a different bf16_chunk signature silently selects conversion. The expr base (expr.hpp, tron's expression interface) decides by comparing member-function pointers: `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)`. Only a MISSING override takes the fallback silently. A mismatched const qualifier, parameter type, return type, an overload set, or a template makes `&B::bf16_chunk` ill-formed or incomparable, which is a compile error. A missing noexcept still compares unequal and the override is used. Factual error: section 8 calls the fallback lossy. The fallback fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)) truncates and only changes bits when the exponent is saturated and the low 16 bits are nonzero; after even_part (shift left 16) or odd_part (mask high 16) the low 16 bits are always zero, so the fallback is bit-exact for stored bf16 and only costs extra instructions. The section-8 check 'exact bf16 copies with independent patterns' therefore cannot detect an omitted override. Round-1 F35's verifier corrections said both of these; the revised handling of F35 kept the wrong sentence.

also.title: 'Different signature silently selects conversion' is inaccurate

votes.reason:
I re-derived both claims from the primary sources and the finding holds.

Claim 1 (design.txt:221, "a different signature can silently select conversion instead"). The expression base decides by comparing member-function pointers: `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)` [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117@2880c3aa9b]. Consumers call through the base reference (`dmatensor(expr<B, N> const& rhs)` ... `rhs.bf16_chunk(i)`) [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:270-276 and 291-296@2880c3aa9b], so that comparison is instantiated for any new row type. When B declares no member named bf16_chunk, `&B::bf16_chunk` names the inherited base member, the pointers are equal, and the fp32 conversion branch is chosen with no diagnostic. When B declares a same-named member with a different function type, there is no composite pointer type, so the comparison is ill-formed (C++ [expr.type]/4, no clause covers different function types). I confirmed this with g++ 11.4 `-fsyntax-only` on a minimal copy of the expr pattern (stdin, nothing written): omitted member and differently named member -> fallback branch taken silently; non-const, `int` parameter, different return type, overload set, member template, and static member -> compile errors ("comparison between distinct pointer types ... lacks a cast", "address of overloaded function with no contextual type information", "invalid operands"). The existing overrides in tron use exactly the plain form: `bf16s bf16_chunk(size_t i) const noexcept` [h/tron/hardware/permuted.hpp:53@2880c3aa9b] and the same with a `requires` clause [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:366-368@2880c3aa9b]. So the design sentence misstates the failure mode: a different signature is loud, and only omission (or a different name) is silent.

Claim 2 (design.txt:398, "silently takes a lossy fallback"). The fallback is `fp32s_to_bf16s(self().chunk(i))` [expr.hpp:115@2880c3aa9b]. `fp32s_to_bf16s` ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field equals 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, then shifts right 16 and narrows [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109@f46e48bab498 for 16 lanes; :55-88 for 8 lanes uses the same mask then keeps bytes 2-3 of each lane]. The design's own chunk(i) contract produces fp32 lanes from the packed bf16 pair by `even_part` (shift left 16) or `odd_part` (mask the high 16 bits) [design.txt:220 and :225; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007@2880c3aa9b], so the low 16 bits of every lane are zero and the NaN correction never fires. The fallback therefore returns the stored bf16 bits unchanged; it costs instructions, not bits. The section 8 check "exact bf16 copies with independent patterns" (design.txt:398) cannot detect an omitted override, and the objdump inspection list at design.txt:440 does not name bf16_chunk extraction.

Round-1 F35 verifier corrections stated both points ("Omitting the member entirely is the only way to get the silent fp32 round trip; a mismatched parameter, return type, or const-qualifier fails ... as a compile error"; "That fallback is bit-exact for stored bf16 values ... so the design's ... check does not detect the omission") [r1-findings.md:341-352, F35 entry]. The revised design's section 9 lists F35 as "Accepted with concrete contracts ... exact bf16 override" [design.txt:467] but kept the wrong failure mode.

The finding's proposed static_assert is sound: with the member omitted, `decltype(&v_vnni_row<...>::bf16_chunk)` is a pointer to member of the expr base, which `std::is_same_v` does not equate with a pointer to member of v_vnni_row, so the assertion fires.

Two small corrections to the finding text, neither of which rescues the design sentence: (1) the word "repeats" is wrong; the original design row read "matrix[token].bf16_chunk(i) | Extract the stored bf16 bits directly. Avoid a float conversion during exact copies." [original design-text.txt:260] and had neither the "different signature" sentence nor "lossy fallback", so both sentences were introduced by the revision (as R90 and R69 say). (2) "A missing noexcept still compares unequal and the override is used" follows the standard's composite-pointer-type rule ([expr.type]/4.6), but g++ 11.4 rejects that comparison ("comparison between distinct pointer types ... lacks a cast"); tron builds with clang 19 (facts-r2.md toolchain line), which I could not run here (no clang on this host). Either outcome is a compile-time result, not a silent fallback, so the finding's conclusion is unaffected.

Qualify the noexcept sub-claim: per the C++ standard a missing noexcept compiles and the override is used, but g++ 11.4 rejects the comparison as distinct pointer types; clang 19 (the tron toolchain) was not tested here. In both cases the result is a compile-time outcome, never a silent fallback.

Both factual claims of N13 hold against the primary source, and no other line of the revised design covers them.

Claim 1 (override detection). The expression base (expr, tron's rank-1 expression interface) picks the override with `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)` [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117@2880c3aa9b; `git diff f46e48bab498 2880c3aa9b -- h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp` is empty]. The design says "a different signature can silently select conversion instead" [design.txt:221]. That is wrong. A stdin-only g++ 11.4 syntax check of the same CRTP pattern (no files written, nothing in the worktree) gives: non-const member, `int` parameter, or wrong return type -> "comparison between distinct pointer types ... lacks a cast" (hard error); overload set or member template -> "address of overloaded function with no contextual type information" (hard error); member omitted -> the fallback branch is selected. So only omission (or a different name) is silent. The error surfaces when expr<B,N>::bf16_chunk is instantiated, i.e. at the first consumer that reads bf16 through the base, e.g. `dmatensor(expr<B,N> const& rhs)` calling `rhs.bf16_chunk(i)` [h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp:270-276@2880c3aa9b]; that is loud, not silent. The design never states that omission is the silent case (grep "omit" hits only design.txt:333, unrelated).

Claim 2 ("lossy fallback"). design.txt:398 says the failure is that the type "silently takes a lossy fallback", detected by "exact bf16 copies with independent patterns". The fallback is fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)). Both variants of fp32s_to_bf16s OR 0x00010000 only where the exponent field == 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits != 0, then shift right 16 and narrow [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:55-88 (8-lane) and :92-109 (16-lane)@f46e48ba; file unchanged at 2880c3aa9b]. The design's chunk(i) produces fp32 by even_part (shift left 16) or odd_part (mask high 16 bits) [h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007@2880c3aa9b; design.txt:220,225], so the low 16 bits are always zero and the fallback returns the original bf16 bits in both builds. A bit-pattern test therefore cannot detect an omitted override; the only consequence is extra instructions. The objdump inspection list [design.txt:440] names V appends, token copies, weighted sums and arena allocation but not bf16 expression reads, so no other row detects it. The round-1 F35 verifier corrections asked for exactly these two fixes [r1-findings.md F35: "Omitting the member entirely is the only way to get the silent fp32 round trip; a mismatched parameter, return type, or const-qualifier fails ... as a compile error"; "bit-exact for stored bf16 values ... so the design's ... check does not detect the omission"; "Add bf16 extraction (bf16_chunk) to the generated-instruction comparison list"].

votes.correction:
Two wording corrections to the finding; the substance stands.

(1) "the revision repeats the claim" and "kept the wrong sentence" are inaccurate. The original design (/tmp/issue4525-design-before.html, 67,216 bytes = the round-1 size in facts-r2.md) contains zero occurrences of "lossy", "silently" or "different signature"; its bf16_chunk row read "Extract the stored bf16 bits directly. Either outcome is loud; neither is a silent fallback, so the correction to the design is unchanged: only an omitted (or differently named) bf16_chunk silently selects fp32s_to_bf16s(chunk(i)), which is bit-exact for stored bf16 and costs a shift, a NaN check and a narrow per chunk; any other signature fails to compile at the first bf16 consumer. I checked both factual claims against the primary source and confirmed them; the finding stands. It also stays inside the intent: Ben asked for typed access, jhan asked for a design, and round-1 F35 asked for the exact override signature. The finding keeps that instruction and corrects only the stated failure mode and the test-detection claim.

Claim 1 (design.txt:221, HTML line 176: "a different signature can silently select conversion instead") is a factual error. expr<B,N>::bf16_chunk (expr.hpp = tron's expression interface) decides with `if constexpr (&B::bf16_chunk != &expr::bf16_chunk)` [h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp:110-117@2880c3aa9b].
