The fallback fp32s_to_bf16s ORs 0x00010000 only where the exponent field equals 0x7f800000 AND the low 16 bits are nonzero, then truncates (srli 16 + narrow in the 16-lane build; byte shuffle of the high halves in the 8-lane build) [h/tron/simd/bf16.hpp:92-109 and :55-88@f46e48bab498; `git diff f46e48bab498 2880c3aa9b --stat` on bf16.hpp and expr.hpp is empty, so the same at live main]. The design's own row read uses even_part (slli 16) or odd_part (and 0xffff0000) [design.txt:220,225; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:2000-2007@2880c3aa9b], so the low 16 bits are always zero and the fallback returns the stored bits exactly. So the section-8 check "exact bf16 copies with independent patterns" cannot detect an omitted override; a compile-time check or the instruction record can.

Claim 3 (round-1 already said this) is confirmed: r1-findings.md F35 has three verifier corrections stating "Omitting the member entirely is the only way to get the silent fp32 round trip", "a compile error, not a silent fallback", and "bit-exact for data that came from bf16". confirmed.section: 5. Interface design (operation contract table)
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity. The reviewer's rule is that a private constructor prevents relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data. confirmed.recommendation: Add to the contract row: "v_vnni_row has the same restrictions: its (pair address, parity) constructor is private, v_vnni_view<T,R,D> is its friend and only producer, it exposes no pointer, and detail::vnni_access is the only pointer reader."

I re-derived the claim from the revised design text, Ben's comment, the round-1 findings and tron's view.hpp. The finding holds.

What the revised design says. The no-relabel rule is stated once, in the contract table row "View copy / conversion": "No public pointer constructor, .data member, or pointer conversion for packed views." [design.txt:222]. The only type the design calls a view is v_vnni_view: "v_vnni_view accesses a packed V matrix. v_vnni_row reads one logical row." [design.txt:43]. Section 5 itself uses "view" and "row" as two different objects: "The row stores its pair address and even/odd position by value. It remains valid after a temporary view object disappears" [design.txt:212]. The word "friend" appears once in the whole design, for detail::vnni_access (the internal raw-pointer accessor) [design.txt:223]; the design never says that v_vnni_view is a friend of v_vnni_row or that the row's constructor is private (grep of design.txt for friend, private, constructor, relabel: lines 61, 63, 212, 222, 223, 277 only). Line 61 "restricted construction of views" has the same "views" wording. The generic Words row "A view accesses those values without owning their storage" could be read to include the row, but that reading conflicts with the design's own row-versus-view usage at line 212, so it does not remove the ambiguity.

Why an implementing agent would guess wrong. The design tells the implementer to keep the row's aliases "consistent with existing views" [design.txt:213]. The existing tron rank-1 view is a struct with a public pointer member `T* data;` and a public constructor `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr) noexcept : data(data) {}` [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:116-126 @f46e48bab498]. The rank-2 view builds its row as `return element(data + s0 * i);` [view.hpp:72-75 @f46e48bab498]. Copying that pattern gives v_vnni_row a public (pointer, parity) constructor and a public data member.

Why the harm is real. The design gives writable rows writable element access: "Non-const writable access changes only that element." [design.txt:218]. With a public (pair address, parity) constructor, v_vnni_row<bf16,D>(ptr, false)[i] = x writes ptr[2*i] through any pointer, which is exactly the relabelling Ben's rule forbids: "The private constructor prevents routine callers from relabelling an arbitrary row-major pointer as packed data." [Ben comment 5765866077, github-review.json]. Ben's sketch has no row type at all (no operator[]), so the row is the design's own addition and the rule reaches it only if the design says so.

Not already handled. No round-1 finding covers the row's constructor: r1-findings.md mentions v_vnni_row only for the rename (F-naming), const-row indexing (view.hpp:146 precedent), the bf16_chunk override, and the child's k_vnni_row write rule. Section 9 of the design therefore makes no claim about it.

The fix is one sentence in the contract table; production code paths (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token) are unaffected; the risk is a silent breach of Ben's access rule that a reviewer would catch late. One nuance for the recommendation: a const v_vnni_view<bf16,R,D> must produce v_vnni_row<const bf16,D> [design.txt:218 "Const matrix access yields a read-only row"], so the friend declaration must cover the whole v_vnni_view family (all T), not one instantiation.

What the design says. The pointer-construction restriction appears once, in the contract table: "No public pointer constructor, .data member, or pointer conversion for packed views" [design.txt:222]. The general retain list says "restricted construction of views" [design.txt:61]. The row is described only as "v_vnni_row reads one logical row" [design.txt:43], "v_vnni_row<T,D> inherits expr<row_type,D>" [design.txt:211], and "The row stores its pair address and even/odd position by value" [design.txt:212]. No sentence says who constructs a v_vnni_row or that its constructor is private. The reviewer questions (design.txt:80-85) and the "Explicitly deferred" paragraph (design.txt:277) do not mention row construction, so this is not a flagged deliberate choice.

The Words table defines a view generically ("A view accesses those values without owning their storage" [design.txt:31]), which would include the row; but the "Proposed V types" row and the declarations name only v_vnni_view a "view" and call v_vnni_row a row [design.txt:43, 198-200]. The existing rank-1 and rank-2 view types are structs with a public `T* data;` member and a public `explicit constexpr view(T* data = nullptr)` constructor [h/tron/tensor/view.hpp:36-44 and :116-126 @2880c3aa9b]. The finding holds. I checked each piece of evidence in the primary sources.

(1) The revised design's wording is packed-only. design.txt:257 reads "page::scaled_v, detail::scaled_v_expr | Keep the page method. Give the expression constructor a typed packed V view." The original design said "Give scaled_v_expr, the existing weighted V sum, a typed V input" (build-neutral; extracted from /tmp/issue4525-design-before.html, step "4. Weighted V sum").

The design keeps that: design.txt:270 "Keep row-major V in the 8-lane cache" and design.txt:322 "Keep native K and 8-lane V as their existing arrays." So an implementer cannot literally give the 8-lane scaled_v_expr constructor a "typed packed V view"; a v_vnni_view over row-major storage would compute wrong addresses.

(3) The 8-lane constructor today also takes a raw pointer. kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:2139-2142 (`#else` branch): `scaled_v_expr(const tensor<page_size>& scales, const bf16s* data, const size_t count, tensor<head_size>& scratch)`. The shared member `const bf16s* const data;` is at line 1992, outside the `#if`. Both builds are fed from page::scaled_v at line 2261: `scales, kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).v[0], count(), scratch`.

(4) The design nowhere names the 8-lane constructor's input. grep of design.txt for scaled_v finds only lines 180, 257, 316, 353, 360, 395, 463. design.txt:316 says "Obtain the physical address only inside the typed implementation" and describes "the 8-lane row-major path", which implies a typed input for both paths, but names no type. design.txt:255 says page::v_tensor returns "the packed or row-major view selected by the build" but never connects page::scaled_v to v_tensor. Lines 257 (packed only) and 316 (typed for both paths) therefore conflict for the 8-lane path, so the implementing agent must guess. That is a real kind (c) ambiguity.

(5) Terminology part: design.txt:257, 283, 306, 316 use "live-token count"; the Words used here list defines only "Valid token row" (design.txt:45). The design never names page::count() (grep for "page::count" and "count()" in design.txt: no hits), although round-1 F42's verifier corrections asked for "count (passed as page::count())" [r1-findings.md:411, 413]. So the only ways to honor the finding are (a) k_vnni_view is not an expr in the child (at() plus typed bulk operations, as in Ben's straw-man) or (b) the design names a consumer and a test. The finding's recommendation is option (a).

Why the fairness lens does not refute it: the design does not defer the K row expression (the deferred list [design.txt:63, 275] is parent scope and keeps expression reads), and the only deliberate-choice flag is the generic reviewer question "May the view provide operator[] as well as at(token, dimension)? Yes. The expression interface requires row indexing." [design.txt:86]. That question does not say why the child's K type needs expression reads or who consumes them, so the finding's no-caller evidence is not answered by the design.

Corrections to the finding:
1. The finding misstates the design's rule. design.txt:63 reads "Limit the parent: expression reads and existing row operations. Defer slices, iteration, generic expression assignment, and expression constructors until a caller needs them." Expression reads are explicitly kept, not deferred. The argument should instead be: the design gives no reason, consumer, or verification row for extending the expression-read requirement to the child's K type.
2. The finding omits the textual root of the design's choice. Ben's review #2 (posted on PR 4424, whose new raw pointers are the VNNI-K plane pointers) asked to "follow the precedent already present in tron: ... tensor and dtensor which provide a uniform interface based upon expr" and to give the type "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations that we need here" [evidence/github-review.json, review 5270587330]. Ben's later straw-man #3 has at() only and "no data(), pointer conversion, or operator[] that suggests a contiguous row" [same file, comment 5765866077]. The finding should say the design must choose between Ben's #2 (expr) and #3 (at() only) for K and record that choice, rather than imply the requirement has no source.
3. "adds cost without a consumer" should read "adds implementation and test cost without a consumer"; there is no runtime cost, because no hot path would call chunk(i).

Recommendation stands: either name the consumer of a K row expression (and add a Child-only verification row for it) or state that k_vnni_view is not an expr in the child (at() plus typed store_row/load_row/store_block and the typed plane argument, as in Ben's #3), keeping load_row (the gather) as the typed row read. A 16-dimension chunk read would be an 8-dword gather across 8 lines 64 bytes apart [k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:101-124]; the cost at issue is implementation and test effort, not runtime.

votes.reason:
Short version: the finding's facts hold (no child code reads a VNNI-K row through expr, and the design mandates a K row expression), but its stated basis misreads the design's deferral rule, and it omits the uniformity rationale that the design took from Ben's comment #2. The finding is partly right; it is not refuted.

Facts I checked and that hold:
- The mandate exists. design.txt:369 (child list item 4): "Define k_vnni_tensor, k_vnni_view, and its row expression in h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp."
- Dense AMX QK path passes the whole plane: h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1437-1439 `qk_vnni_128x4(pg.template k_vnni_plane<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head), q_packed, ...)`.
- Partial-page software path passes the whole plane to qk_group: self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1635-1639.
- The child's software loop explicitly has no row view for VNNI slots: self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1594-1603, comment "A VNNI slot has no row view" and `return 0;  // no row view: the VNNI plane has no contiguous rows`; the `keys[i]` row read at :1625-1626 runs only in the `else` (row-major) branch.
- FPGA staging uses get_k_row into caller scratch: h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655.
- Page copies use gather_row + scatter_row: kv_cache.hpp child diff c7844ca2ce..30c4ac82cb hunk at 1930/2096 (`k_vnni::gather_row(` then `k_vnni::scatter_row(`; file line 2111 at the child).
- Every test caller in the child reads K rows through set_k_row/get_k_row or k_vnni::gather_row (git grep at 30c4ac82cb: t/t_llama_unit.cpp, t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp, t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp); none indexes a VNNI-K row through page::k or an expr.
- Cost claim: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cb:25-29 gives plane[(((s*4+c)*16+dp)*16+t)*2+j]; for fixed (s, c, t), consecutive dimension pairs dp are 32 elements (64 bytes) apart, so one 16-dimension chunk is 8 dwords in 8 different 64-byte lines. gather_row (:218-228) already does this as "4 gathers of 16 dwords". So a K row chunk() would be a strided dword gather, as the finding says.
- dotter, the software query/key dot-product helper, accepts only contiguous views (facts-r1: kernels/dotter.hpp:16-82 takes sseq<1> views), so a K row expression could not feed the one plausible expr consumer without a scratch copy.

Where the finding is wrong or incomplete:
1. Misread rule. The finding says "The parent's own rule defers expression features until a caller needs them" citing design.txt:63. That line reads: "Limit the parent: expression reads and existing row operations. Defer slices, iteration, generic expression assignment, and expression constructors until a caller needs them." Expression READS are in the kept set; only slices, iteration, assignment and constructors are deferred. A K row expression is an expression read, so line 63 does not support deferring it.
2. Omitted intent. The design makes rank-2 expression access a deliberate decision for Ben's comment #2: design.txt:56 "Keep rank-2 expression access and logical row reads", design.txt:84 "May the view provide operator[] as well as at(token, dimension)? Yes. The expression interface requires row indexing." Ben's comment #2 (review 5270587330, verbatim in github-review.json) asks to "follow the precedent already present in tron: ... types like tensor and dtensor which provide a uniform interface based upon expr" and to give the type "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types". That comment was written against PR 4424's K pointers, so the K type is the original target of the expr-uniformity request. Deferring the K row expression while V keeps one would make K the only typed cache tensor without expr access. The finding does not weigh this.
3. Parity with V. The parent's V row expression also has no production caller at main (facts-r1: V readers at f46e48ba are set_v, v_data, scaled_v, get_v; none builds a tensor from a page). Round-1 F08 kept V's row expression anyway as "the one cheap usual tensor operation" (r1-findings.md F08 recommendation). The finding's real differentiator is cost (V chunk = one 64-byte load plus shift/mask; K chunk = 8-line dword gather), which it states but does not frame as the reason to treat K differently.
4. Round-1 lineage. Round-1 C05's recommendation sentence reads "k_vnni_row offers the same logical interface as vnni_row (expr<row, D>, chunk(), bf16_chunk(), set())" (r1-findings.md C05). The revised design's line 369 follows that. N35 relates itself only to F08 and does not say it reverses part of C05.

Why not refuted: Ben's own straw-man (comment 5765866077) has at() only and says "There is no data(), pointer conversion, or operator[] that suggests a contiguous row", so Ben's intent on expr is open, and the design itself holds it as a pending question (design.txt:84). The finding's recommendation is an either/or that leaves the design free to justify keeping the row expression. The consequence is real but small: an implementing agent following line 369 would write a gather-based k_vnni_row with no consumer, and line 369 gives no mechanics for it, so the agent would also have to invent chunk() and bf16_chunk() for K.
votes.correction: Design decision, partly right (child scope). Facts: no child code reads a VNNI-K row through expr (dense and partial QK take the whole plane [self_attention.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1437-1439, 1635-1639]; the software loop states "no row view" for VNNI slots [:1594-1603]; staging uses get_k_row [full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655]; copies use gather_row + scatter_row [kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2111]; all tests use set_k_row/get_k_row), and a K row chunk would be an 8-line dword gather. Corrections to the finding's argument: design.txt:63 keeps expression reads and defers only slices, iteration, generic assignment and expression constructors, so it does not support deferring a K row expression; the design mandates the K row expression for uniformity with V under Ben's comment #2 ("uniform interface based upon expr"), recorded as a decision at design.txt:56 and as an open question to Ben at design.txt:84; V's row expression likewise has no production caller and was kept by round-1 F08 as the cheap "usual tensor operation"; round-1 C05 recommended a k_vnni_row with expr<row, D>. Corrected recommendation: in child item 4 (design.txt:369), tie the K row expression to Ben's answer on the operator[]/expr question (design.txt:84). If Ben accepts expr access, keep it and add one sentence: k_vnni_row::chunk() is an inspection/test read (one dword gather across 8 lines per 16 dimensions, built from the gather_row pattern), and hot paths (staging, page copies, QK) use load_row, store_row, store_block and the whole-plane kernel arguments, never the row expression. If Ben declines expr access, drop the K row expression together with V's. Either way, state the choice; do not leave "its row expression" as a bare requirement.

confirmed.title: No method for 'collected and executed' evidence; lane can skip tests
confirmed.section: 7. Implementation steps and files (step 7) and 8. Verification and acceptance (CI ownership; Definition of done)
confirmed.claim: Omission and ambiguity: the design requires the implementer to record that the required suite collected and executed the new cases, and AGENTS.md makes that verification mandatory before committing a test, but the design names no place to look and does not warn that the required GCP Nix lane can report "Test host" green without running any test. The lane sets RUN_TESTS false when the exact test-runtime identity already has an NFS passage marker, and only a GitHub rerun forces execution. An implementer who reads a green check as execution evidence records a false claim.
confirmed.evidence: design.txt line 358 ("Record the required suite's collected and executed cases"), line 423 ("new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence"), line 452 ("Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage"). AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24: "Before committing it, verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient." .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 `RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}`, :544-590 every test step `if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'`, :675-698 "Mark exact test identity passed" / "Verify cached test identity" via bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py. README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588: "An empty NFS passage marker records that one exact test-runtime and test-environment pair passed both executor jobs. The first workflow attempt may reuse that marker; a GitHub rerun always executes the host and FPGA tests."
confirmed.design_quote: Run the applicable commands in section 8. Record the required suite's collected and executed cases. Preserve the separately tracked AMX CI gap.
confirmed.recommendation: Add to step 7 or the CI paragraph: "Evidence of execution is the GCP Nix `Test host` job log of a run whose test steps ran (RUN_TESTS true: first attempt with a changed test runtime, or a GitHub rerun), showing Slice executing t_llama_unit and t_heterogeneous_scheduler with the new case names. A green `Test host` whose steps were skipped by a cached passage marker (README.ci.md 'Result Reuse') is not execution evidence. Record the run URL and attempt number."

The CI mechanism the finding cites is verbatim: AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 ("verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient"); .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 `RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}`, every test step 543-590 guarded by `if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` while the checkout at 540 is unguarded, so the job reports success with all test steps skipped; README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588 and :154-155 ("A rerun executes tests even when the same runtime already passed"). Round 1 never raised this (no hits for passage/run_attempt/RUN_TESTS/Result Reuse in prior-review.txt, r1-findings.md, facts-r1.md), so the revised design has not dispositioned it. What does NOT hold is the risk sentence "records a false claim": bin/ci/tron-build/prepare_handoff.py@2880c3aa9b:41-45,56 sets tests_required false only when has_passed finds a marker keyed by the exact source hash (hash over every tracked blob, gcp-nix.yml:489) and the exact build+environment closure (bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:30-51); that marker is written only by mark-passed in the Test job (gcp-nix.yml:675-686), which runs only when tests_required was true and after bin/ci/tron-build/require_results.py:10-20 confirmed test-host and test-fpga both succeeded. So a reused-marker green Test host means the identical test binary already executed and passed in an earlier run; the statement "collected and executed" stays true, only the cited run's log would show no execution. Also, every parent commit touching h/ or t/ changes both the source hash and the build closure, so attempt 1 on each new head executes the tests; reuse arises only for an identical tree (re-triggered workflow, merge-queue run with the same tree). The finding's recommendation detail "showing Slice executing ... with the new case names" is unverified (I did not check whether tron-test-host prints Catch2 case names).
votes.correction: Omission/ambiguity (kind c/d), minor: design step 7 (design.txt:358) and the CI paragraph (:423, :452) require the implementer to record required-suite collection and execution evidence but name no artifact, and the run-tron-tests skill they point to (:429) covers only local logs and `make list-tests`. Drop the sentence "An implementer who reads a green check as execution evidence records a false claim": the GCP Nix passage marker (test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:30-51) is written only after both executor jobs ran and passed for the identical source hash and build closure (gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:671-686, require_results.py:10-20), so a reused-marker green Test host has execution evidence in an earlier run; the risk is citing the wrong run's log, not asserting something untrue. Reduced recommendation: add one sentence to step 7 or the CI paragraph naming the artifact, for example "Evidence is the GCP Nix Test host job log of a run whose test steps ran (RUN_TESTS true: first attempt on a new tree, or a GitHub rerun); a run that reused a passage marker (README.ci.md 'Result Reuse') shows skipped steps, so cite the earlier run that executed the identical closure. Record the run URL and attempt number." Note that the parent's own code commits always change the identity, so attempt 1 on each new head executes.

votes.reason:
Checked every piece of evidence in the finding against the primary sources; all of it holds, and the revised design does not cover the point anywhere.

Design quotes are exact: design.txt line 358 "Run the applicable commands in section 8. Record the required suite's collected and executed cases."; line 423 "new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence or the user's explicit exception."; line 452 "Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage." A grep of design.txt and of the HTML page for rerun, re-run, passage, "Result Reuse", "run URL", RUN_TESTS, "run attempt", "job log" returns nothing. The nearest design sentences are line 403 "Never count a placeholder success or a hardware-unavailable early return as execution of the feature. [S12]", line 425 "A green disabled-feature test is insufficient", line 431 "Report skipped checks by name", and line 429 "Read the repository's run-tron-tests skill". None names where execution evidence comes from, and none mentions the cached-passage skip. The section 9 row "F16 C08 Coverage gap separated from scope" is about the AMX flag gap, not about evidence of execution. The design does not flag this as a deliberate choice or a reviewer question.

The run-tron-tests skill the design points to does not fill the gap either: its CI line (SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:63-64) says to run the affected bin/ci test and lint, and "make coverage-report-t_<name>" (line 68) is local coverage, not CI execution evidence.

AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 reads verbatim "Every committed test must run in CI. Before committing it, verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient."

The skip mechanism is real. .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 sets `RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}` on the test-host job (name "Test host", lines 532-533); every step after checkout is guarded by `if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` (lines 544, 547, 559, 564, 569, 572, 575, 582, 590). tests_required comes from prepare_handoff.py (lines 41-45, 56) via test_runtime.tests_required (test_runtime.py:70-74: `return run_attempt > 1 or not already_passed`). The final "Test" job (gcp-nix.yml:661-662) runs "Mark exact test identity passed" (675-676) when tests were required and "Verify cached test identity" (687-688) otherwise, both through bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py. README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588 reads verbatim "An empty NFS passage marker records that one exact test-runtime and test-environment pair passed both executor jobs. The first workflow attempt may reuse that marker; a GitHub rerun always executes the host and FPGA tests." README.ci.md:644-646 repeats this under "Forcing Re-run".

So the omission is real, the warning is correct, and the recommendation (name the Test host job log of a run whose steps ran, record run URL and attempt) is consistent with the repository's own documentation. Severity minor matches: it does not change what gets built, it affects the quality of the process evidence the design itself demands.
votes.correction: One precision to add to the finding, not a refutation. The passage marker is keyed by three things, not only the test-runtime identity: a source key (first 7 hex characters of sha256 over `git ls-files -s`, the tracked-file index, excluding compile_commands.json) [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:486-489], plus the test-runtime and test-environment store paths [test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:30-36, 45-51: root / source_key / f"nix-tests-{identity}.passed"]. Any change to a tracked file therefore produces a new marker path, so the first CI attempt after a real code or test change executes the tests. Reuse happens when an identical tracked tree is run again within the three-day marker lifetime [README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:509]: a commit-message-only amend, a rebase that changes no file content, or a re-push of the same tree. The finding's recommendation should say this, and should add the visible sign of reuse: in the "Test host" job every step after checkout shows as skipped, and the final "Test" job runs the step "Verify cached test identity" instead of "Mark exact test identity passed" [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:675-698].

votes.reason:
The finding's evidence holds and its core claim stands; one nuance narrows the failure scenario.

Design text checked. The revised design makes execution evidence a deliverable in three places without saying what form it takes or where it comes from: "Record the required suite's collected and executed cases" [design.txt:358], "Confirm collection and execution of each changed behavior case" [design.txt:411], "new tests cannot be committed without required-suite execution evidence" [design.txt:423], "Required tests collect and execute the new behavior coverage" [design.txt:452]. A grep of design.txt for "log", "logs", "attempt", "reuse", "marker" and "rerun" finds no hit. The design does point the implementer at the run-tron-tests skill [design.txt:429]; that skill names the LOCAL Slice log directory ("Slice logs are under logs-$(hostname)/latest/" [.agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b, last paragraph]) but says nothing about CI execution evidence or result reuse. So "names no place to look" is slightly overstated for local runs and exactly right for the CI side.

Repository rule checked. AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 reads verbatim: "Every committed test must run in CI. Before committing it, verify that a required CI suite collects and executes it; local execution and the test file's presence are not sufficient."

CI mechanism checked. .github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538 sets `RUN_TESTS: ${{ needs.tron-build.outputs.tests_required == 'true' || github.run_attempt > 1 }}`; every test step of the Test host job carries `if: env.RUN_TESTS == 'true'` (541-590), while the checkout and cleanup steps run unconditionally, so the job reports success with all test steps skipped. The Test job then runs "Mark exact test identity passed" (676-684) or "Verify cached test identity" (688-696) through bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py. README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588: "The first workflow attempt may reuse that marker; a GitHub rerun always executes the host and FPGA tests." Also :154-155 and :644-646 ("Rerunning a host or FPGA test job executes its tests even when ... its original handoff reused an exact passage marker").

Nuance the finding omits (see correction). The passage marker is keyed by the source hash as well as the runtime identity: passed_sentinel returns root / source_key / f"nix-tests-{identity}.passed" [test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:45-51], source_hash = sha256 of `git ls-files -s` over the whole tracked tree [gcp-nix.yml:489], identity = sha256 of the test-runtime and test-environment store paths [test_runtime.py:30-36], tests_required = run_attempt > 1 or not already_passed [test_runtime.py:70-74]. Therefore the first attempt of any push whose tracked tree has not already passed always executes the tests. Reuse can only occur for a merge_group run (trigger at gcp-nix.yml:15) whose merged tree equals an already-passed PR tree, or for a re-push of an identical tree. The false-claim scenario is real but narrower than "the lane can skip tests" suggests.

Intent lens. The finding does not move the design away from Ben's request (typed tensor access, comments #2/#3) or jhan's request ("Another agent will implement the design by reading this file", codex-add-tensor-type.md); it adds a process detail that AGENTS.md already mandates and that has no effect on Ben's acceptance. Round-1 F16/C08 asked for the AMX coverage gap to get an owner and a reference to issue #3997 (r1-findings.md:95-110, 164-172) and did not ask for an evidence method, so this is a new round-2 omission, which is allowed. Because the design's Definition of done names the evidence as a deliverable without a form, an implementing agent would have to guess; that is kind (c)/(d) with low consequence, so minor is the right severity.
votes.correction: Omission and ambiguity: the design requires the implementer to record that the required suite collected and executed the new cases [design.txt:358, 411, 423, 452] and AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:22-24 makes that verification mandatory before committing, but the design names no CI-side source for that evidence and does not warn that the required GCP Nix "Test host" job reports success with every test step skipped when the exact source hash plus test-runtime identity already has an NFS passage marker [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:538, 541-590, 676-696; test_runtime.py@2880c3aa9b:45-51, 70-74; README.ci.md@2880c3aa9b:586-588]. Because the marker key includes the source hash of the whole tracked tree [gcp-nix.yml:489], the first attempt of any newly pushed commit executes the tests; the skip applies to a merge-queue run of an unchanged tree or a re-push of an identical tree. The recommendation stands: name the Test host job log of a run whose test steps ran (RUN_TESTS true) as the evidence, record run URL and attempt number, and state that a green Test host with skipped steps is not execution evidence.

confirmed.title: Guard description omits other-user and blackout refusal conditions
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Commands and execution hosts)
confirmed.claim: Factual imprecision: the design says campaign_guard_acquire "checks the CI lease and takes a lock between this user's campaigns" and says to "stop if CI takes the host" when ci_took_dut returns busy. ci_took_dut is ci_lease_busy OR other_user_active OR blackout_active, and campaign_guard_acquire additionally refuses when a runtron process is running and when rinzler serving is active unless the caller passes --allow-serving. Its flock reserves the machine only among this user's own sessions. also.title: ci_took_dut also covers other users and blackout

confirmed.title: -DAVX512=ON silently overridden on host without AVX-512
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Build configurations, Commands and execution hosts)
confirmed.claim: Omission: the 16-lane rows pass -DAVX512=ON to preset native, but that preset keeps BUILD_NATIVE on, and CMake probes lscpu and sets AVX512 OFF with only a warning when any required feature is missing, so on a build host without AVX-512 both '16-lane' rows silently become 8-lane builds. The design names sw-dev-01 as the build host without stating whether it has AVX-512, and does not name the cross-avx512 preset that exists for this case.
confirmed.evidence: CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:38 'option(BUILD_NATIVE "Probe this host before enabling AVX512" ON)'; :95-116 'if (BUILD_NATIVE) ... foreach(FEATURE ${REQUIRED_AVX512_FEATURES}) if(NOT ...) set(AVX512 OFF) message(WARNING "Disabling AVX512: ${FEATURE} not supported")'; CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:41-49 preset cross-avx512 'Cross-compile for AVX-512 from a non-AVX-512 host' with BUILD_NATIVE OFF, AVX512 ON; design.txt:411-412, 430.
confirmed.design_quote: cmake --preset native -DAVX512=ON -DTRON_AMX_DISPATCH=OFF
confirmed.recommendation: Add one sentence under Build configurations: 'Confirm the configure log contains no "Disabling AVX512" warning. On a host without AVX-512, configure with -DBUILD_NATIVE=OFF (preset cross-avx512) for the 16-lane rows; those binaries can only run on an AVX-512 host.'

votes.correction: The omission holds, but the mechanism sentence over-reaches. Only the "16-lane, AMX code off" row (design.txt:411) can silently become an 8-lane build. The "16-lane, AMX code on" row (design.txt:412) cannot degrade silently: the TRON_AMX_DISPATCH definition does not depend on AVX512 (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:219-224, 329-332), and h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp@2880c3aa9b:30-36 has `#if defined(TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) && TRON_CHUNK_SIZE != 16` followed by `#error "TRON_AMX_DISPATCH requires TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 ..."`, so that row fails at compile time on a host where the probe turns AVX512 off. Corrected claim: "Omission: the 16-lane rows pass -DAVX512=ON to preset native, which keeps BUILD_NATIVE on; CMake probes lscpu and sets AVX512 OFF with only a configure-log warning when a required feature is missing. On a build host without AVX-512 the AMX-off row silently becomes an 8-lane build, and the AMX-on row fails with a #error. The design names sw-dev-01 as the build host without stating that it has AVX-512, and does not name the cross-avx512 preset (BUILD_NATIVE OFF, AVX512 ON) that exists for this case." Inside the Owner& overload (slice.hpp:38-42) `owner` is a named lvalue, so `owner.as_view()` selects the lvalue-qualified as_view() (the deleted rvalue forms at design.txt:210 do not fire), and the resulting prvalue view can bind only to the generic expr overload (a non-const prvalue cannot bind Owner&; it is not a view/const_view/const_views specialization). That overload captures the temporary view by reference, and the temporary dies at the end of the return statement in slice.hpp:41. So passing ANY packed owner, lvalue or temporary, through slice<>(owner, ...) yields a dangling reference, whereas an ordinary tensor owner is safe today because its as_view() returns a view<> that the by-value overload at slice.hpp:53 copies. confirmed.title: cmake preset flags vs make targets: cache caveats unstated
confirmed.section: 8. Verification and acceptance (Build configurations; Commands and execution hosts)
confirmed.claim: Ambiguity: the design gives three `cmake --preset native -D...` configurations and then says to run `make build-test` and `make test-host`. Those Make targets reconfigure gen/ with Make's own preset choice and flag list, which never mentions AVX512 or TRON_AMX_DISPATCH; the hand-passed values survive only as CMake cache entries in gen/. On an AVX-512 host (sw-dev-01 is one: Ryzen 9 9950X passes the probe's six features) this works, but on a host without AVX-512 Make selects cross-avx512, whose preset forces AVX512=ON over a hand -DAVX512=OFF, and refuses to run tests. The `native` preset also pins binaryDir to gen/, so the three configurations cannot be three build directories in one checkout; each needs a full reconfigure or its own worktree. The Nix lane uses BUILD_NATIVE=OFF, so `cross-avx512` is the closer local equivalent of the required lane than `native`.

The child code confirms this: k_vnni.hpp@30c4ac82cbb6:139-147 scatter_row issues 4 dword scatters of one token's lanes and touches no other token. The design also chose separate V and K families with separate owners (design.txt:62 "one concrete view per layout"; design.txt:82, a listed reviewer question), so no generic code will call one overload set on both layouts; a shared verb buys nothing technically.

3. The "would mean different things" claim is inaccurate and the mapping is explicit. page::append_v (kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1866-1920) and append_v_row share the identical partner rule (even destination zeroes, odd preserves, lines 1877-1919 comments "store [0 b]" / "store [b d]"); both write one token into the packed V plane and differ only in source form (packed page vs contiguous row). The design maps each existing page method to exactly one typed operation: design.txt:252 "page::set_v ... Forward to append_v_row. save_v_impl -> page::set_v -> append_v_row"; design.txt:256 "page::append_v Keep the name; call copy_token."; design.txt:303 "Production packed-V row writes use page::set_v or page::append_v. Both call the typed append/copy operations." An implementing agent has no guess to make. The finding's "in the same header" is also imprecise: append_v_row lives in h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp (design.txt:241, 350) and page::append_v in kv_cache.hpp.

4. The finding's own cited memory rule cuts against its first option. vnni-k-terminology.md (jhan 2026-09-15): "save = the operation ... store = the CPU instruction only". A V operation named store_row would deviate from that rule; append_v_row avoids the word. The rule is for prose and kept code identifiers like store_k_block, so it does not forbid Ben's name, but it gives no support for forcing "store" onto V.

5. Round 1 already accepted the name. r1-findings.md F38 verifier correction recommends "add a three-row mapping table (Ben store_row -> append_v_row + set_pair and row.set; Ben load_row -> load_row; Ben store_block -> child PR only)". The revised design did exactly that at design.txt:229 (store_row -> append_v_row), 233 (load_row kept), 379 (store_block, child). prior-review.txt:253, 387, 1791 show the round-1 review itself used append_v_row as the accepted name of the save operation. Objecting in round 2 to a name that round 1 endorsed is not a defect in the revision.

What is not covered is only a one-clause nicety (page::append_v and append_v_row share the partner rule and differ in source form), which the table rows at 252/256 already make unnecessary for the implementer. Residual severity: note, no change required.

The finding is a naming preference with no consequence for the implementing agent or for Ben's acceptance, and two of its supporting claims are wrong.

(1) "Renamed ... unasked" misstates the history. The ORIGINAL design already used append_v_row (round-1 extraction design-text.txt:310 "Keep an internal operation named append_v_row to write a newly added cache row", :321, :334). The round-1 review used and endorsed that name: F01's recommendation reads "the cache-append operation (append_v_row: on an even token it writes the even row and zeroes the odd row ...)" (r1-findings.md:4-15), and F38's verifier correction asked for "a three-row mapping table (Ben store_row -> append_v_row + set_pair and row.set; Ben load_row -> load_row; Ben store_block -> child PR only)" (r1-findings.md:361-370). The revision did exactly that: design.txt:229 "append_v_row is this design's name for the sketch's V store_row" and design.txt:233 load_row. So the append_v_row / load_row pairing the finding objects to is the round-1 recommendation carried out. The finding pushes against that recommendation without saying so.

(2) "append_v and append_v_row would mean different things in the same header" is wrong on both counts. Both carry the same cache rule: design.txt:229 (append_v_row: even destination zeros its odd partner, odd preserves) and design.txt:243 (copy_token "moves the four even/odd branches of today's append_v. An even destination zeros its partner. An odd destination preserves it."). The source agrees: kv_cache.hpp@f46e48bab498:1867-1870 "Even-destination paths zero the odd partner", and Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots] :2063-2064 lists append_v and set_v together under the same invariant. design.txt:303 groups them explicitly: "Production packed-V row writes use page::set_v or page::append_v. Both call the typed append/copy operations." The two names also live in different headers: append_v_row goes to h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp (design.txt:241, step 1 at :352), page::append_v stays in kv_cache.hpp (:256, step 5 at :355). The finding's recommended sentence "page::append_v ... is unrelated to append_v_row" would therefore be false.

(3) No consequence for the implementing agent. Name, file, callers and mapping are all explicit: design.txt:229, :232-236, :241, :252 ("save_v_impl -> page::set_v -> append_v_row"), :354. The K names are equally explicit in the child section (:378-379). Nothing is left to guess.

(4) No consequence for Ben's acceptance. Ben labelled his text "an API sketch, not a compiled implementation" and "a straw-man ... a starting point" (comment 5765866077, evidence/github-review.json). His comment #2 asked for "the row-wise load/store operations that we need here", i.e. the operations, not their identifiers. The design's reviewer questions (design.txt:82-85) cover semantic deviations from the sketch (formula placement, const rule, operator[], scope), which is what round-1 F02 required; F02 did not list the name. A function name is changed in one commit at code review.

(5) The verb asymmetry with K has a stated basis: design.txt:383 "K stores differ from V stores ... it must never read, merge, and rewrite a whole 64-byte line." K has no partner rule, V does. The existing code already mixes verbs for the same V rule (page::set_v and page::append_v, kv_cache.hpp:2063-2064), so adopting store_row for V would add a third verb, not remove one. The finding's own cited memory rule (vnni-k-terminology, jhan 2026-09-15: "save = the operation, store = the CPU instruction only") argues against its option 1.

What survives is a cosmetic observation: the V family (append_v_row / load_row) and the child K family (store_row / load_row) use different store verbs, and the design does not say in one sentence that the verb difference tracks the partner rule. That is worth a note at most.

rejected.title: Array placement-new contradicts linked C09 warning; no-cookie rule unstated
rejected.section: 6. Behavior the implementation must preserve (Arena construction without clearing) and 9. Disposition (F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 row)
rejected.claim: Ambiguity: the design prescribes the array placement form `::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[block_count];`, and that form is correct, but the round-1 page it links under [C09] says the array form 'may consume unspecified extra bytes' and should not be used. The disposition row marks C09 'Accepted' and the design gives no basis for overriding that warning, so an implementing agent reading both documents must guess. The basis is: the `void*` placement argument selects the library function `operator new[](std::size_t, void*)`, which C++20 and later exempt from array allocation overhead (CWG 2382, [expr.new]/17 in N4950); independently, the Itanium C++ ABI stores no array cookie when the element type is trivially destructible and has no two-argument class-scope operator delete[], which is Clang's rule as well. The design already requires trivial destruction of the block (design.txt:328) but does not connect that requirement to the array form, and it does not ask for a static_assert on the trait or a check that the arena byte count is a whole number of blocks.

votes.reason:
Short version: the "contradiction with the linked C09 page" does not exist. The page the design links under [C09] prescribes the same array placement-new form the design uses, and the warning against that form lives only on a votes sub-page one link further away. The technical basis the finding wants stated is correct, but two of its three "omission" sub-claims are also wrong, so what remains is a note-level polish, not an ambiguity.

Words used here: array placement-new = the C++ form `::new (p) T[n]` that creates n objects at an address p that is already allocated. Array cookie = a hidden element count a compiler may store in front of such an array. kv_block = the struct holding one KV head's K and V data for one page. C09 = round-1 finding "Construction pass needs the slot-spec loop".

1. Factual error in the finding's headline claim. The design's two [C09] citations point at claude-review-design-new-tensor-type.html#C09 (2 hrefs in status/design-new-tensor-type.html). That page's C09 entry carries only Claim, Evidence, Recommendation and Found-by text, and the phrase "unspecified extra bytes" appears nowhere on that page [prior-review.txt:1465-1497; grep count 0 for the phrase in prior-review.txt]. The same linked page prescribes, in its own "Recommended edits" item 7, exactly the design's form: "Replace 'placement construction' with the exact form: ::new (static_cast<void*>(region_base)) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages]; per storage slot region, no parentheses or braces" [prior-review.txt:1794]. Round-1 F12's recommendation on the same page also offers `::new (region_base) kv_block_t[n_kv_heads * n_pages];` as an accepted alternative [prior-review.txt:459-463; r1-findings.md F12 Recommendation]. The warning the finding quotes is one verifier's refinement 3(b) on the votes sub-page (status/claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html#C09, reached from the C09 entry's "votes and corrections" link) and in r1-findings.md, which the design does not link. The round-1 lead's synthesis did not adopt that refinement. So the design followed the linked page's instruction; an implementing agent reading the design and its linked page sees one form, not two. The disposition row "F12 F40 F56 C01 C09 | Accepted; array extent clarified" [design.txt:468] matches what the design took from C09: the per-slot extent and loop [design.txt:331-333].

2. The finding's technical basis holds (this part is not refuted). With g++ 11.4.0 at -std=gnu++2b -O2 (the only compiler on this host; the pinned clang 19 is not installed here), `::new (p) T[n]` for a trivially destructible T returns p with offset 0 (`xorl %eax,%eax; ret`), emits no memset and no loop, and returns offset 0 even for a type with a user-declared destructor; the only extra code is the bad_array_new_length bound check. That matches the C++20 exemption for the library `operator new[](std::size_t, void*)` (CWG 2382) and the Itanium ABI no-cookie rule for that placement form. I could not run the pinned clang 19; Clang's code generation also skips the cookie for the reserved global placement operator new[], but that is from memory of Clang's source, not tested here.

3. Sub-claim "does not ask for a static_assert on the trait" is partly wrong. The design requires trivial default construction, copyability and destruction for owner and block [design.txt:328] and asks the t_llama_unit test row to "Check block size/offset/alignment contracts and trivial type traits" [design.txt:399]. Only the placement of the check (next to the construction rather than in a test) is unstated.

4. Sub-claim "does not ask for a check that the arena byte count is a whole number of blocks" asks for a tautology. make_kv_slot_offsets computes block_bytes = KV_BLOCK_PLANES_2 * 64 * sizeof(bf16) * head_size and slot_bytes = n_kv_heads * block_bytes with checked multiplies [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:651-667]; block_bytes equals sizeof(kv_block<64, head_size>) by the existing static_assert [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1316-1318]; the arena byte count is n_pages times the per-page unit [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1165-1167]. For uniform geometry every slot has the same head_size, so the arena byte count is a multiple of sizeof(kv_block_t) by construction. The design's "checked arena byte count divided by sizeof(kv_block_t)" [design.txt:331] is therefore exact. AGENTS.md discourages assertions derived from the same data under test [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:39-41].

5. Other cited facts check out: kv_block holds only bf16s arrays [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2190-2202]; bf16x8/bf16x16 are __m128i/__m256i aliases [h/tron/simd/types.hpp@2880c3aa9b:25-27]; allocate_kv_group has no divisibility check [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1199-1208]; the design says "Verify the construction form with the pinned compiler" [design.txt:337].
votes.correction: Note (omission, no change required): the design prescribes one construction form and the linked round-1 page prescribes the same form, so the implementer does not have to choose. The finding says that after `gh pr edit 4424 --base <parent-branch>` "the PR diff shows the old child head against the parent branch, which includes the parent's changes reversed". That describes a two-dot diff. GitHub does not use one for pull requests: "Pull requests on GitHub show a three-dot diff", which compares "the most recent common commit of both branches (merge base) and the most recent version of the topic branch", and "a three-dot comparison keeps showing the changes introduced by the topic branch since the branches diverged" [docs.github.com, About comparing branches in pull requests, fetched 2026-09-22]. The parent branch is built "on a fresh branch from fetched main" [design.txt:344], so it descends from live main 2880c3aa9b. The merge base of the child head 30c4ac82cb and 2880c3aa9b is c7844ca2ce [git merge-base, tron-VNNIed-K]. The three-dot diff c7844ca2ce..30c4ac82cb is 25 files, 2082 insertions, 145 deletions, which is exactly the child's own change set, and it is what #4424 shows today with base main. The two-dot diff the finding assumes (2880c3aa9b..30c4ac82cb) is 119 files, of which 94 are main's changes appearing reversed [git diff --stat / --name-only, tron-VNNIed-K]. So retargeting before pushing the rebuilt branch changes nothing in the displayed diff. The PR's mergeability state does not worsen either: it is already CONFLICTING / DIRTY against main today, draft, label Skip benchmarks, 22 commits [gh pr view 4424, read-only].

(b) The recommended reorder is the harmful one. If the rebuilt jhan-amx-vnniK (which contains the parent's commits) is pushed while #4424's base is still main, the merge base becomes the parent's fork point on main and the three-dot diff then shows the parent's commits inside #4424. That is the mixed-diff failure round-1 F14 described: "If the child is rebased onto the parent branch while its GitHub base stays main, the #4424 diff will show the parent's commits as well as its own" [r1-findings.md:198]. The design's order (step 1 retarget, then steps 2-6 rebuild, then step 7 after the parent merges) [design.txt:366-372] is the order that avoids this window. The finding does not say that its reorder trades a harmless interval for a harmful one.

(c) The rest of the recommendation is already in the design. "Preserve the old head (tag or branch)" is stated: "Preserve the old child head locally before replacing any branch history" [design.txt:364]. "Keep it draft" is stated at step 1 [design.txt:366] and matches the AGENTS.md stack rule "Keep every descendant draft" [AGENTS.md:12-13@2880c3aa9b]. The `--base` flag exists [gh pr edit --help line 27], as the finding itself concedes.

(d) Not an ambiguity. The design gives an explicit numbered order; an implementing agent would not have to guess. Intent check: Ben's comments do not touch PR sequencing; jhan asked for "#4424 to be atop the new PR" [codex-add-tensor-type.md, action plan item 4]; round-1 F14 recommended exactly "once the parent PR is open, change #4424's base to the parent branch (gh pr edit 4424 --base <parent-branch>), rebase the child onto that branch, keep it draft" [r1-findings.md:200]. The revised design follows that recommendation in that order.

Residual, at most a note: the child steps never say the word "push" for the rebuilt branch; the push is implied between step 6 and step 7. That was not the finding's claim.
votes.correction: The design's order (retarget #4424 to the parent branch first, then rebuild and force-push the child) is the order that keeps #4424's displayed diff equal to its own changes at all times, because GitHub compares from the merge base (c7844ca2ce). Optional one-sentence clarifier for step 1: "GitHub shows the three-dot diff from the merge base, so the displayed #4424 diff is unchanged until the rebuilt branch is pushed; push it only after this retarget."

findings_intro: Eight finders read the revised text through one lens each (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs). Their candidates, plus defects the disposition checkers found in the fixes themselves, were merged and each put to three verifiers who tried to refute it; a finding survived only if at least two could not. A completeness critic then added candidates that went through the same verification. Severities are the lead's final grades; where they differ from the finder's grade, the finding says so under Lead's reading.
questions_intro: Round 1 asked codex to list its departures from Ben's sketch as questions for him instead of asserting them. The revision has a four-row "Questions for the reviewer" table with a proposed answer per row, marked as proposals pending agreement. The table below checks whether the four questions cover every departure and whether an implementer can act on them.
questions_rows: Q1. May the address formula live in each concrete view? Proposed: yes, with separate V and K families and separate owners.
Folding the layout type into the view (Ben's reservation, jhan's reading) and the two-family consequence (no single vnni_tensor<Layout> template).
Right question and right proposed answer. The cost of two families (duplicated conversion and access plumbing) is stated in the answer, which is enough for Ben to weigh it.
Q2. Should a const view object prevent mutation of its elements? Proposed: yes, at both matrix and row rank.
The departure from Ben's std::span rule (round-1 F04).

Right question. The revision now says the repository precedent is mixed (design section 2) and chooses the matrix rule for both new types. It cites only the rank-2 source; the rank-1 comment that states Ben's rule is not linked (N46, note).
Q3. May the view provide operator[] as well as at(token, dimension)? Proposed: yes; at() stays as an equivalent bounds-checked spelling.
The departure from Ben's at()-only access (round-1 F02).

Right question. It should say why the expr base needs operator[] (it indexes rows through it) and why Ben's sketch had no operator[] (a two-argument accessor cannot be spelled with one subscript), so Ben sees the trade (N09, minor).
Q4. Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? Proposed: yes; slices, iteration and generic writes are deferred.
The scope cut round 1 asked for (F08) versus Ben's "usual tensor operations".
Right question. The deferred list in section 5 is concrete. The design should say which sections change if Ben answers no (N07, note).
Missing: who asked for native K in the parent, and does Ben agree?
Typing the native-K kernel parameter goes beyond Ben's sketch, which types only the packed planes. jhan asked for it (prompt item 4, issue #4525).

Design section 2 calls it "the requested parent scope" without naming the requester, in a table whose other rows are Ben's requests. Name jhan as the requester and either add a fifth question or say that jhan owns this decision (N08, minor). All three judges rated the questions block inadequate on this point.

verdict_intro: Three judges read the revised design with the dispositions and the confirmed new findings in hand, each from a different position: the implementing agent, the maintainer who wrote the straw-man, and a risk reviewer. All three returned the same verdict, accept with changes, and all three said the text is not yet implementable without a question to jhan or Ben beyond the four listed ones. All three also judged the questions block inadequate because native-K typing is not put to Ben.

judges.reasons: The 16-lane production path is specified correctly against live main 2880c3aa9b: the save/load/copy chains (design.txt:250-257), the even-append partner-zero rule (:283-305), the scaled_v bounds (:257) and the placement-new arena construction (:322-337) match kv_cache.hpp, so no residual item would silently corrupt attention sums. Four items would still make the implementing agent build the wrong thing or stop to ask: N03 (the child table at design.txt:375-381 never switches detail::kv_block's K member, the per-head K-then-V storage block, from the raw array, which at 30c4ac82cb kv_cache.hpp:2380 is still `bf16s k[...]` and is reinterpret_cast at :1692/:1706/:1730/:1742, so a port as-is breaks Ben's construction rule), N01 with M01 and N61 (design.txt:270 orders packed bodies for both chunk widths and :413 orders 8-lane t_llama_unit runs, but t_llama_unit.cpp:105-108/:483 and :142/:1201-1204 and heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:443 call get_v/set_v unguarded while kv_cache.hpp:1616-1674 declares them only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16), N02 (design.txt:318 and the Bits-and-conversions row give a NaN expectation that holds only in Debug because src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-293 defines TRON_IGNORE_NAN, the switch that disables NaN handling in the SIMD conversion, as a PUBLIC option for every non-Debug configuration, and both the native preset at CMakePresets.json:37 and the Nix test build at nix/cmake-tron-test-build.nix:80 are RelWithDebInfo), and N04 (design.txt:53 says the reviewer questions need no answer now while :463 makes recorded answers a done criterion and names no owner or place). Three repository-rule items are cheap text fixes that must land first: N41 (design.txt:431 lists make iwyu-check as required and omits make lint, but README.ci.md:76-78 requires `Lint` and SKILL.md:65-66 asks for iwyu only for a public API header), N17 (copy_plane at :236/:244/:352 has no caller since kv_cache.hpp:1941/1955/1981 are the only memcpy sites and none copies a whole V plane, which contradicts the design's own defer rule at :63), and N36 (no execution-evidence method for :457-459 and :466, so a cached-passage green check could be recorded as execution). M05 must also be fixed because section 9 (design.txt:485-503) labels 20 partly-addressed ids "Accepted" and claims to include "nine later corrections", and I confirmed the F35, F41 and C01 verifier corrections are not applied (:221 still says a different bf16_chunk signature silently selects conversion, :318 has no build dependence, :333 has no uniform-geometry statement), so jhan would read the round-1 review as closed when it is not. The questions block is incomplete (N08): Ben's sketch section 5 types only packed_k_page and packed_v_page and keeps existing_row_major_k_storage, while the design types the K argument of qk_rowmajor_128x4 (design.txt:262-264), replaces std::span sources with tron row views (:238) and renames store_row to append_v_row (:230), and none of Q1-Q4 (:58-61) carries these departures. Every other new finding and residual is a compile error the agent will hit and fix (N14, M03), a naming or wording gap (N05-N07, N09-N13, N18-N24, N43-N46), a child-scope detail settled later (N30-N35, N55-N58, M07), or a verification-phase note (N37-N40, N60), and can be handled during implementation.
top_three_edits: N03 - add one row to the child adaptation table (design.txt:375-381): "detail::kv_block K member: when k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> holds, the K member is k_vnni_tensor<page_size, head_size> (std::conditional_t with the existing bf16s array). Keep sizeof(k) == sizeof(v), 64-byte alignment and trivial default construction so the parent's placement-new block-array construction covers it. k_view()/k_at() exist only for the array member. The packed-plane accessor (keep k_vnni_plane or use the sketch's k_packed) returns kv_block<geometry>(slot, kv_head).k.as_view(), never a cast of the array (today's casts: kv_cache.hpp:1692, 1706, 1730, 1742 at 30c4ac82cb)."

N01 + M01 + N61 - replace design.txt:270 with: "The class definitions of v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row are complete in both builds (members are a bf16 array, a pointer and small integers). Their operation bodies (append_v_row, load_row, copy_token, chunk, bf16_chunk) and every packed-V test case compile only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16; the 8-lane build implements no pair extraction. The typed kernel declarations and the fake definitions in t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp stay unconditional." Rewrite the 8-lane row at :413 and the line-400 row: "At unmodified main, t_llama_unit (t_llama_unit.cpp:105-108 with :483, and :142 via :1201-1204) and t_heterogeneous_scheduler (heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:443) do not compile in this configuration, because page::set_v and page::get_v exist only under TRON_CHUNK_SIZE == 16 (kv_cache.hpp:1616-1674). The 8-lane check for the parent is: configure, build the tron library and t_amx_dispatch_dtype, run t_amx_dispatch_dtype. Do not count t_llama_unit or t_heterogeneous_scheduler results in this row." Remove the 8-lane expectation from the t_llama_unit behavior rows.

N02 - after the TRON_IGNORE_NAN sentence at design.txt:318 add: "TRON_IGNORE_NAN is defined for every non-Debug configuration (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt:292-293, a PUBLIC option of tron). The native and deb presets and the required Nix test build are RelWithDebInfo, so in every configuration in section 8 both paths truncate identically (0x7F800001 -> 0x7F80 on both). The 0x7F81 result appears only in the Debug presets asan, tsan and coverage." In the section 8 row "Bits and conversions" add: "NaN expectations for the generic path depend on TRON_IGNORE_NAN; either guard them with #ifdef TRON_IGNORE_NAN or check the generic path only with finite, denormal and infinity inputs, which convert identically in both paths."

verdict_outro: I agree with the judges. The 16-lane production path, which is the path that ships, is now specified correctly against live main: the save, load and copy chains, the partner-zero rule, the scaled_v bounds, the arena construction form and the lease rules all match the source. Nothing in the residual list would silently corrupt an attention sum. The four majors are about the 8-lane configuration, a test expectation, the child's K storage, and process; each is a one-paragraph edit.

Must change before implementation starts: edits 1 to 5 in section 7 (N04 and N08; N01 with M01 and N61; N03; N02; M05). Everything else can be fixed while implementing, and the implementer should treat the partly rows of section 3 as a checklist.
rejected_intro: These candidates were refuted by at least two of the three verifiers. They are listed so a reader can see what was considered and why it did not hold; the votes page carries the full reasons.
method: This round ran as one workflow of 268 agents (about 29.7 million tokens, 4,716 tool calls, 1 hour 51 minutes). Every agent read the same verified-facts files (round-1 facts and a round-2 addendum I verified myself against live main 2880c3aa9b before the run) and had read-only access to the tron worktree at the pinned commits, Ben's comments, jhan's prompts, the round-1 findings and the revised design text.

Disposition phase: 15 batches of related round-1 findings (2 to 4 ids each). One checker per batch graded each id and reported any new defect the fix introduced; two adversarial re-graders (source-truth, fairness) re-graded every id; the majority decided. 45 agents. Result: 35 resolved, 20 partly, 3 deferred, no split votes.

New-defect phase: 8 finders (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs) produced 81 candidates; the checkers added 17 more; a merge agent grouped the 98 into 62. Three verifiers per candidate tried to refute each one; 56 survived and 6 were rejected (section 9). A completeness critic added 8 candidates, and all 8 survived the same verification, for 64 new findings. Three judges then gave independent verdicts.

Limits. Nothing was compiled or run; the claim that the two test programs do not compile in the 8-lane build (M01, N61) is inferred from the #if guards in the source, not from a build. The design's pinned links were re-validated structurally (every local target exists; the 38 GitHub blob links are the same set as in round 1) but not fetched. This page was checked for pure ASCII, for an anchor per round-1 id, and for resolving local links; no browser render check was run on this host.
method_bullets: Data and scripts: evidence/claude-review-r2/ holds workflow-result.json (every agent's return value), findings.json (the data behind this page), build_findings.py and gen_review.py (the generator), overrides.json (my grades and prose), lead-verified-facts-r2.md (the facts I verified before the run), r1-findings-compact.md (the round-1 findings as the agents read them), design-revised-text.txt and design-revised-sha256.txt (the exact text reviewed).

Votes: every new finding's three votes and corrections are on [the round-2 votes page](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-votes.html); the disposition votes are inside the rows of section 3 (expand "Votes and evidence").

Round 1: the original review is archived as [claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r1.html) with its data in evidence/claude-review/. The revised design cites its ids; the anchors on this page keep those links working.

State at review time (2026-09-22 04:00 to 06:15 UTC): main 2880c3aa9b; PR 4424 draft on main at 30c4ac82cb, no reply after Ben's sketch; issue #4525 open, assigned to jhan, 0 comments, body unchanged since 00:11 UTC; issue #3997 open.

Severity re-grades by the lead after reading the votes: N12 to note (two of three verifiers: an omission of the 8-lane rule, not a wrong statement); N07 and N42 to note (the majority of their votes). The four majors kept their grade: N01 (two verifiers said minor on its own, but with M01 and N61 the 8-lane guidance as a whole would send the agent into a baseline compile failure), N02, N03, N04.
